sections.heading: 1. Kill defective evidence before it becomes a defective complaint
paragraphs: The first trap is treating an outlier as a false claim. CMS Part B utilization, Part D prescribing, Open Payments transfers, and SAM.gov awards describe different units, reporting periods, and legal relationships. A high reimbursement total may reflect specialty mix, a referral center, or reassigned billing rather than fabricated services. Build cohorts by specialty, geography, service code, and reporting year before ranking providers. Preserve downloaded bytes, release notes, retrieval timestamps, and SHA-256 digests with Python hashlib; never overwrite an earlier release with a corrected file. Require a second analyst to reproduce every material total from the frozen source. An illustrative investigation trigger is a peer-adjusted result above the ninety-ninth percentile with at least thirty comparable observations, but that trigger supports research, not an allegation. Stop dossier delivery when a material identifier join lacks documented corroboration or a suppressed cell has been treated as zero. Track reproducibility as accepted calculations divided by tested calculations, targeting 100% for cited exhibits. The operator sells a defensible analytical process; counsel decides whether the facts support falsity, knowledge, materiality, and a federal payment nexus. A clean chart without those elements is an expensive visualization, not litigation inventory.

The second trap is assuming public-data synthesis automatically creates an eligible relator. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4), substantially the same allegations or transactions disclosed through specified public channels can expose an FCA action to dismissal unless an exception applies or the Government opposes dismissal. The original-source analysis is substantive: timestamped downloading alone does not establish independent knowledge that materially adds to disclosed allegations. FOIA production is not a magic originality certificate. Maintain a disclosure chronology separating public records, independently obtained observations, voluntary government disclosures, and the proposed complaint date. Counsel should also evaluate first-to-file exposure under § 3730(b)(5), recognizing that sealed competing cases may prevent definitive clearance. The third trap is pleading aggregate suspicion without the circumstances required by Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 9(b). Build a representative-claim matrix with claimant, date, payment program, alleged false statement, supporting record, and missing factual links. Circuit standards differ; representative claim examples are not a universal mechanical prerequisite. Measure claim-link completeness against counsel's jurisdiction-specific checklist rather than inventing missing invoices. If public records cannot support the required inference, stop the complaint workstream and offer a bounded research engagement instead of manufacturing certainty.

The fourth trap is treating a seal as an ordinary confidentiality label. FCA complaints must be filed through licensed relator counsel under the statutory seal, served with the required disclosure on the Government, and withheld from the defendant until the court orders otherwise. The initial statutory period is sixty days; extensions can produce investigations lasting years. Keep matter names out of shared sales systems, invoices visible to unrelated customers, public repositories, and external AI prompts. Use counsel-controlled storage, role-based access, encrypted transfer, and a named recipient list for every export. One unauthorized external disclosure triggers an immediate distribution stop, evidence preservation, and counsel-led response. A seal breach can cause sanctions and imperil participation, but State Farm v. Rigsby rejects automatic dismissal for every violation; do not promise either inevitable forfeiture or automatic forgiveness. The fifth trap is acquisition misconduct: borrowed credentials, unauthorized portal access, restricted patient exports, and fabricated corroboration can overwhelm an otherwise useful analysis. Record acquisition authority separately from factual relevance. A record's usefulness does not authorize obtaining it. Quarantine questionable material without further circulation, preserve access logs, and let counsel determine lawful handling and any required remedial steps before analysis resumes.

callout.title: Make the evidence packet survive an adversarial reread
callout.body: Experienced teams optimize for reproducible contradictions, not the largest anomaly count. These practices reduce paid rework before counsel commits to a filing.
items: Attach a source-release identifier and SHA-256 digest to each exhibit so later CMS revisions cannot silently change the alleged pattern.
Keep a disconfirming-evidence worksheet alongside the accusation theory; require analysts to test specialty mix, ownership changes, and billing reassignment.
Ask counsel for the jurisdiction-specific Rule 9(b) checklist before purchasing additional datasets, then price only the research needed to close identified gaps.
Use neutral matter codes on contractor invoices and maintain the identity mapping only in counsel-authorized storage with restricted access.

sections.heading: 2. Reconcile cash without borrowing against a sealed hypothesis
paragraphs: The sixth trap is booking alleged damages, Government recoveries, or projected awards as operator revenue. Formula v2.0 fixes annual gross operator revenue at $95,000, $487,500, and $880,000; corresponding cost ceilings are $64,600, $268,125, and $369,600. Subtraction produces $30,400, $219,375, and $510,400 of annual owner net profit at 32%, 45.0%, and 58% margins. A transparent illustrative allocation uses no award receipts: Conservative has five $1,500 monthly retainers plus $5,000 of completed projects; Base has eight $5,000 monthly retainers plus $7,500 of completed projects; Scaled has ten $7,000 monthly retainers plus $40,000 of completed projects. These allocations explain the supplied totals without claiming the scorecard prescribed customer counts. Each assumes twelve paid months and earned service delivery. An advance retainer can create a contract liability until performance occurs. Under ASC 606, principal-versus-agent analysis determines gross or net presentation for pass-through services. Never include client claim value, merchant turnover, or federal contract value in this revenue line. Maintain separate ledgers for earned retainers, collected cash, refundable advances, reimbursable costs, and realized award proceeds; reconcile them monthly before describing the business as profitable. Revenue visibility and available cash are related measurements, not interchangeable balances.

The seventh trap is financing payroll with contingent percentages. FCA shares generally run 15%–25% when the Government proceeds and 25%–30% when it does not, subject to statutory adjustments and exclusions. SEC and CFTC programs generally use 10%–30% ranges for qualifying awards; IRS § 7623(b) generally uses 15%–30%, with eligibility thresholds and reduction rules. These are distinct programs, not one universal 15%–30% entitlement. An analytics vendor has no automatic right to a relator's award or counsel's legal fee. State professional-conduct rules, including restrictions on sharing legal fees with nonlawyers, must shape engagement design. Price ordinary research as documented services rather than assuming a percentage arrangement is permissible. For sensitivity analysis only, a $1,000,000 recovery multiplied by a 20% eligible share equals a $200,000 award before applicable deductions. If counsel's valid fee agreement absorbs 40% and reimbursable case costs equal $20,000, the illustrative retained amount is $100,000 before taxes. That amount belongs only to the legally entitled recipient. It contributes zero to this operator's budget unless entitlement, measurement, and receipt are established. An unfavorable judgment, dismissal, ineligibility determination, or failed collection instead produces zero award revenue after years of work.

The eighth trap is hiding delivery leakage inside attractive headline margins. In the illustrative Base allocation, eight clients consuming thirty analyst hours monthly require 240 hours before selling, management, and quality control. At a $75 blended delivery cost, that is $18,000 monthly, leaving $4,343.75 from the Base monthly cost ceiling of $22,343.75 for all other expenses. The canonical 1 FT + 2 C team therefore needs explicitly contracted capacity; headcount alone does not prove deliverability. An extra eight hours per client each month adds $57,600 annually, cutting owner profit from $219,375 to $161,775 if prices remain unchanged. Trigger scope revision when delivery hours exceed 110% of the signed allowance for two consecutive months. Suspend discretionary enrichment when an undisputed invoice exceeds forty-five days, subject to the engagement's notice terms. Require a thirteen-week cash forecast excluding all prospective awards. Three months of the Base total cost ceiling is $67,031.25, above the $10,000–$45,000 startup range; deposits, staged hiring, or a smaller initial footprint must bridge that gap. The stated $1,500–$9,500 monthly operating-expense range does not replace fully loaded scenario costs. Refund obligations and committed contractor payments remain cash exposures even when revenue collection stops.

sections.heading: 3. Price dismissal, award denial, and platform exclusion explicitly
paragraphs: The ninth trap is interpreting DOJ non-intervention as either vindication or automatic defeat. Non-intervention leaves a relator to proceed under § 3730(c)(3), usually with heavier financing and litigation burdens; it is not itself a merits judgment. Government dismissal under § 3730(c)(2)(A) is a separate event. The Granston memorandum describes dismissal considerations, not a statutory recovery entitlement or a portable probability table. United States ex rel. Polansky v. Executive Health Resources addresses Government dismissal after intervention, including later intervention, and the applicable procedural framework. Build an illustrative cohort of twenty counsel-screened matters: six stop for public-disclosure or pleading defects; fourteen proceed; three receive intervention and eleven do not. Assume two of those eleven later face Government dismissal, leaving nine privately pursued matters. The model's non-intervention rate is 11/14, or 78.6%; its assumed Government-dismissal rate among non-intervened matters is 2/11, or 18.2%. These are planning inputs, not reported DOJ or Granston rates. If one intervened and one privately pursued matter ultimately collect, eighteen of twenty produce zero recovery. Replace every assumption with counsel's documented cohort experience when available, preserving the denominator and observation window so incompatible rates cannot be multiplied together.

The tenth trap is treating submission as award eligibility. SEC Form TCR and IRS Form 211 serve different statutory programs and require distinct evidence, identity, timing, and award procedures. Route both through counsel under this operating model. An anonymous SEC submission requires attorney representation and additional identification procedures before payment; a generic anonymous email does not substitute for the prescribed process. Monitor SEC Notices of Covered Action because an award application generally must arrive within ninety calendar days of the notice. IRS mandatory-award eligibility generally requires proceeds in dispute exceeding $2,000,000 and, for an individual taxpayer, gross income exceeding $200,000 for at least one taxable year at issue. Tax return information remains subject to statutory confidentiality restrictions. Track each program's filing receipt, declaration, supplemental submission, notice date, and application deadline independently. Distinguish denial before payment from recoupment after payment. False statements, disqualifying conduct, revised proceeds, invalid entitlement, or contractual disputes can create reductions or repayment exposure depending on the governing rule or agreement. Never assert a universal clawback period. Preserve award determinations, fee calculations, cost invoices, and correspondence so counsel can reconcile actual retained proceeds rather than reverse-engineering them from an optimistic press release.

The eleventh trap is converting data access into an adversarial contest with the source platform. Repeated rate-limit violations, shared API credentials, scraping behind revoked access, and concealed account replacement can cause permanent account exclusion or contractual liability. Use documented CMS downloads, approved API access, permitted Open Payments exports, licensed import-manifest datasets, and authorized SAM.gov interfaces. Cache immutable public releases instead of repeatedly retrieving identical records. Set a local operational pause after three consecutive HTTP 429 responses, honor Retry-After, and resume only within published access conditions. A revoked credential or explicit access denial triggers an immediate stop, not credential rotation to defeat the restriction. Separately, monitor false-positive burden: if more than 20% of a twenty-item reviewed sample fails basic entity or arithmetic validation, disable that scoring rule until corrected. Keep safety thresholds distinct from legal conclusions. A 19% defect rate still does not justify forwarding a known error. External enrichment also creates disclosure risk when query strings contain sealed defendant names or protected identifiers. Strip sensitive fields before authorized enrichment and use a counsel-approved offline workflow where stripping would destroy context. The fallback is slower legitimate research, not a disguised replacement account or a purchased credential.

callout.title: Four pre-flight verifications before a dossier leaves the workspace
callout.body: A failed verification stops external delivery. Preserve the work already performed, identify the defect, and resume only after the responsible person documents its resolution.
items: Verify acquisition authority, immutable source copies, and reproducible exhibit totals; quarantine every restricted record lacking a documented access basis.
Obtain counsel's public-disclosure, original-source, first-to-file, and jurisdiction-specific pleading assessment without claiming inaccessible sealed dockets have been cleared.
Verify recipient permissions, seal-sensitive fields, and the exact filing or award-application deadline before transferring any matter package.
Confirm the engagement remains solvent with zero award receipts, documented contractor capacity, and cash reserved for refunds and committed delivery.

sections.heading: 4. Remove procurement pass-through defects and rehearse the shutdown
paragraphs: The required mapped play, gsa_municipal_set_aside_facility_ghost_brokering, is workable only as disclosed coordination between an eligible facility-service prime and qualified subcontractors. The name must not become an operating instruction to conceal who performs the work. Consider an illustrative $100,000 eligible service contract: a documented $5,000 coordination fee less $3,200 of delivery costs leaves $1,800 contribution before overhead. The operator records only the earned $5,000 service fee, not the prime's $100,000 contract revenue. A cost-of-personnel or similarly situated entity analysis under applicable federal limitations on subcontracting must follow the actual solicitation and 13 CFR § 125.6; the label coordinator does not excuse prohibited pass-through performance. Federal service set-asides generally restrict payments to nonsimilarly situated subcontractors to 50% of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, subject to applicable rules and exclusions. Municipal programs can impose different certification, performance, and disclosure requirements. Verify the specific local ordinance and solicitation rather than transplanting federal percentages. Match capability, licenses, staffing, and required status before quoting. The forensic business must also screen conflicts before accepting investigative work involving its own coordination customers, subcontractors, or counterparties with overlapping records.

The twelfth trap is disguising a success commission as routine coordination while ignoring procurement restrictions. For covered federal contracts, FAR Subpart 3.4 and applicable clauses address contingent fees for obtaining Government contracts, with defined exceptions that counsel must evaluate. A fee is not permissible merely because an invoice says consulting. False eligibility certifications, fabricated subcontractor capacity, sham invoices, and undisclosed kickbacks can expose participants to payment recovery, termination, exclusion, and other liability. Track eligibility evidence by bid date, subcontractor status by performance period, and performance payments against the applicable limitation. An unverified certification or projected prohibited payment allocation stops the bid. If the $5,000 coordination fee is refundable upon a valid contract defect and $3,200 has already been spent, returning the fee changes the engagement from $1,800 contribution to a $3,200 loss. That $5,000 adverse swing must fit the refund reserve. The required fallback is to withdraw noncompliant bids and operate as a disclosed subcontractor on unrestricted work. Do not repackage the same ineligible arrangement under another entity. Keep this play's fee ledger separate from forensic retainers and award proceeds; its illustrative economics are not additional revenue silently added to the canonical volume scenarios.

The thirteenth trap is continuing because sunk research costs feel recoverable. Implement a weekly exception meeting using one ledger for evidence defects, another for delivery economics, and a third for deadlines and access incidents. Assign an accountable person and a next review date to every exception. Red conditions include unauthorized disclosure, missing acquisition authority, fabricated support, a prohibited procurement arrangement, and insufficient cash for committed obligations. Amber conditions include disputed scope, declining paid utilization, and evidence needing corroboration. Counsel owns legal determinations; the operator owns collection pauses, cost freezes, and accurate reporting. Rehearse a zero-recovery quarter in which the largest retainer pauses and no contingent proceeds arrive. In the Base allocation, losing one $5,000 monthly client for three months removes $15,000 revenue before any cost adjustment. If costs remain fixed, annual owner profit falls to $204,375. Reforecast immediately instead of waiting for an annual margin report. Close an engagement with a source inventory, delivered-work acceptance record, outstanding invoice schedule, refund calculation, and counsel-directed retention instructions. Never delete records to make an incident disappear. The durable advantage is surviving enough ordinary paid engagements to pursue exceptional matters without pressuring analysts to turn uncertainty into allegations.

sop_steps.title: Freeze the defective workstream
sop_steps.action: Pause affected collection, external delivery, or bidding immediately.
sop_steps.detail: Preserve source files, permission records, correspondence, and access logs. Do not broaden the pause to unrelated authorized engagements unless the incident affects their evidence or systems.

sop_steps.title: Assign authority and quantify exposure
sop_steps.action: Send the factual incident record to the responsible counsel and operator.
sop_steps.detail: List affected recipients, deadlines, earned fees, refundable balances, committed contractor costs, and potential award dependencies. Separate established facts from unresolved hypotheses.

sop_steps.title: Rebuild the zero-award cash forecast
sop_steps.action: Update thirteen weeks of collections, refunds, payroll, and contracted spending.
sop_steps.detail: Remove every prospective statutory award. Apply the actual engagement terms to service pauses and refunds, and identify the funding needed before any new commitment.

sop_steps.title: Resume with evidence or execute the fallback
sop_steps.action: Document corrected authority, calculations, recipients, and engagement scope.
sop_steps.detail: Resume only the corrected activity. If a procurement bid remains noncompliant, withdraw it and pursue disclosed unrestricted work; if evidence remains insufficient, close the allegation workstream.

chapters.pull_quote: A sealed theory cannot pay payroll, and an unexplained anomaly cannot carry a complaint.
action_checklist: Reproduce every cited CMS, Open Payments, SAM.gov, or manifest calculation from a frozen source release with a recorded SHA-256 digest.
Give counsel a disclosure chronology, acquisition-authority ledger, and jurisdiction-specific claim matrix before expanding any allegation.
Separate earned retainers, refundable advances, reimbursable costs, collected cash, and realized award receipts in the monthly reconciliation.
Run a thirteen-week cash forecast with zero award proceeds and test the loss of the largest retainer for three months.
Implement source-access pauses, recipient checks, SEC notice monitoring, and counsel-owned filing deadlines with documented backup responsibility.
Verify the disclosed facility-coordination play's eligibility, compensation, and subcontracting allocation; withdraw defective bids and use the unrestricted-work fallback.

chapters.question_prompt: Where do high-margin deals, clients, or undervalued assets hide in data-mined qui tam, sec & irs whistleblower analytics, and what repeatable outbound/inbound sourcing system lands the first 3-to-10 wins (4–12 months)?
chapters.title: Sourcing, Demand Mining & Landing Your First Deals
chapters.subtitle: CMS Cohorts, SAM.gov Intent Signals, Rule 9(b) Evidence Packs, and Counsel Retainers Under 31 U.S.C. § 3730
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #48, Data-Mined Qui Tam, SEC & IRS Whistleblower Analytics, ranks #16 of 49 with a 92/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its 11 mapped plays turn public-record anomalies and counsel demand signals into bounded, paid forensic assignments rather than speculative accusations. Mine CMS cohorts, procurement records, import manifests, and agency filings; qualify the evidence; then sell reproducible litigation-support work to specialist firms. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $30,400 Conservative, $219,375 Base, and $510,400 Scaled. Keep those operating plans independent of uncollected statutory awards, which can take 2–5+ years and produce nothing. This chapter supplies sourcing lanes, qualification thresholds, outreach arithmetic, evidence controls, and a 4–12-month path toward the first three to ten paid wins.

sections.heading: 1. Mine eleven sourcing lanes, but sell an evidence workflow rather than an accusation
paragraphs: Build two separate queues: a signal queue containing reproducible anomalies, and a buyer queue containing firms with demonstrated demand for forensic capacity. Use eleven mapped sourcing plays: CMS Part B cohort analysis; CMS Part D prescribing analysis; Open Payments relationship mapping; federal procurement performance analysis; state and municipal procurement analysis; import-manifest reconciliation; SEC disclosure reconciliation; IRS referral preparation; FOIA corroboration services; relator-counsel demand mining; and government_rfp_subcontractor_brokerage. These are working acquisition lanes, not eleven independent promises of recoveries. Start with two adjacent lanes, such as Part B and Open Payments, so the same entity resolution and specialty taxonomy support multiple assignments. Download CMS public-use files with their documentation, preserve release dates, and distinguish provider identifiers from corporate parents. Compare like specialties, places of service, geography, and patient mix before ranking billing intensity. A high percentile is a screening result, not proof of a false claim. Suppression, beneficiary complexity, ownership changes, and coding revisions can create false positives. Sell a fixed-scope cohort validation and source-provenance package that counsel can evaluate without receiving patient records or any sealed material. Record negative findings because eliminating weak leads is itself a billable deliverable when the engagement specifies it.

For federal procurement, join SAM.gov notices and amendments to USAspending award records, then verify performance allegations against the underlying contract, modification history, and acceptance documents. A contract ceiling is neither actual expenditure nor operator revenue. State and municipal boards reveal rebids, repeated extensions, specialized translation needs, courier routes, and understaffed IT projects; each may support either analytics demand or a separate service opportunity. Import manifests require special restraint: commercial access terms, confidential treatment, incomplete consignee information, and freight-forwarder identities limit what can be concluded. Reconcile a shipment hypothesis with authorized invoices and customs records before estimating duty exposure. SEC lanes begin with EDGAR filings and dated disclosure changes; IRS lanes begin with a concrete tax issue and records lawfully available to the prospective source. Neither lane justifies soliciting stolen files. FOIA requests should target specific record series, custodians, and date ranges, with an explicit budget for fees and delay. An illustrative $2,500 source-validation sprint capped at twenty delivery hours yields $125 billed per delivery hour before overhead. If corroboration fails, deliver an auditable rejection memorandum instead of stretching a pattern into an allegation. Counsel still receives a usable decision and a reusable research trail.

The required government_rfp_subcontractor_brokerage play has a different economic engine and must remain separate from whistleblower award assumptions. Scan SAM.gov, state portals, and municipal bid boards for janitorial, grounds, courier, translation, and IT staffing solicitations with thin documented competition. Automated extraction should capture insurance, wage requirements, site visits, bonding, evaluation criteria, and subcontracting restrictions; a human verifies the solicitation and every amendment. On a $100,000 service contract, a $75,000 subcontractor quote leaves a 25% management spread before supervision, insurance, rework, and financing costs. It is not a 25% net margin. A 15–30% spread means fulfillment consumes 85–70% of the customer price before those additional costs. Under covered small-business service set-asides, 13 CFR § 125.6 generally limits payments to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities to 50% of the relevant government payment, subject to applicable exclusions and contract specifics. Do not force the illustrative $75,000 arrangement into an incompatible award. The fallback is an unrestricted commercial or municipal opportunity, with its own rules checked, or qualified similarly situated teaming. Resolve conflicts before investigating an entity connected to a fulfillment client. This optional brokerage lane contributes no revenue to the chapter's forensic scorecard reconciliation.

callout.title: Preserve the information advantage without manufacturing a case
callout.body: Experienced operators monetize clean elimination decisions, reproducible joins, and counsel time saved.
items: Archive each CMS release and its data dictionary together; compare equivalent periods before labeling a provider's billing trajectory exceptional.
Use FOIA tracking numbers as workflow identifiers, never as evidence that an agency has validated the underlying allegation.
Create a public-source demonstration with unrelated or synthetic entities; reserve client-specific facts for the retained firm's restricted workspace.
Ask procurement partners for written fulfillment quotes before calculating spreads, and test similarly situated status against the actual solicitation.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify counsel demand and separate interesting anomalies from viable assignments
paragraphs: Build the buyer list from firm practice pages, publicly unsealed docket entries, published opinions, attorney conference appearances, and analyst hiring notices. CourtListener helps discover matters; confirm important procedural facts in the official docket and never attempt to uncover sealed identities. Select firms that repeatedly handle the same subject matter as the proposed dataset, rather than every firm mentioning whistleblowers. A recent unsealed healthcare matter, a procurement practice expansion, or a posting for a damages analyst is a demand trigger, not evidence of available budget. Maintain separate fields for public source, date observed, practice fit, named business contact, and outreach status. Use a one-hundred-point qualification score: twenty-five points for domain fit, twenty for lawful evidence access, twenty for a concrete paid scope, fifteen for budget and decision authority, ten for delivery timing, and ten for security readiness. Advance scores of seventy-five or more, nurture scores from fifty-five through seventy-four, and archive lower scores. Hard exclusions override the number: requested seal disclosure, unauthorized access, witness pressure, fabricated claims, or payment conditioned on improper legal-fee sharing. A small firm with an immediate bounded research need may outrank a prestigious firm without an identified buyer.

Evidence qualification belongs beside commercial qualification, not after the sales call. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4), substantially similar public disclosures can require dismissal unless the government opposes dismissal or an applicable exception, including original-source status, applies. Counsel must evaluate the disclosure categories, timing, and the prospective relator's independent knowledge; a public dataset anomaly alone does not establish eligibility. Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 9(b) requires fraud allegations to be pleaded with particularity, and circuit standards differ concerning representative claims and reliable indicia. Build a representative-claim worksheet where available: actor, date, service or contract obligation, claim identifier, amount, alleged falsity, payment connection, and supporting source. Do not invent missing claim details from aggregate CMS totals. Record whether the client can lawfully supply supporting documents and whether counsel considers the available specificity adequate. For each lead, maintain an alternative-explanation column covering coding changes, contract amendments, statistical suppression, and entity-resolution errors. Charge for testing those explanations. The fallback for a weak case hypothesis is a paid methodology or data-quality assignment only if the firm independently values that work; otherwise close the lead. A failed theory should not become a recurring invoice without a useful contracted purpose.

Budget statutory upside as a separate, long-duration scenario tree. FCA investigations may extend 2–5+ years under seal, although the statutory initial seal period is at least sixty days. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(b)(2), counsel files the complaint under seal and follows service restrictions and subsequent court orders. Non-intervention does not itself end a case: a relator may continue under the governing provisions. Government dismissal under § 3730(c)(2)(A), associated with the Granston policy and later case law, is a separate branch. Track observed rates only with dated, comparable cohorts and explicit denominators. For sensitivity testing, assume seventy of one hundred hypothetical matters receive non-intervention, then seven of those seventy face government dismissal: 70% and 10% conditional rates, not published DOJ statistics. Apply independent zero-recovery outcomes to failed merits, collection problems, eligibility defects, and unsuccessful continued litigation without double-counting branches. For operating cash planning, set every uncollected award to zero. Seal breaches create severe litigation and eligibility risks, but their consequences are case-specific rather than an automatic universal forfeiture rule. SEC Form TCR and IRS Form 211 submissions also go through counsel in this workflow, with program-specific eligibility and timing checks before any filing.

callout.title: Four checks before accepting sensitive material or a paid mandate
callout.body: Complete these checks with the retaining firm before moving from public demonstrations to matter-specific work.
items: Confirm source ownership, access permission, applicable restrictions, and whether any court order limits possession, use, service, or disclosure.
Have counsel assess § 3730(e)(4), Rule 9(b) particularity, prospective relator eligibility, and whether representative-claim detail can be supported.
Document the client, economic buyer, deliverables, payment terms, conflicts, and absence of unauthorized referral compensation or legal-fee splitting.
Separate paid service revenue from contingent awards, restrict matter access, and budget zero collections from every pending statutory filing.

sections.heading: 3. Run a restrained multichannel cadence that converts research into paid mandates
paragraphs: Use a six-touch, twenty-one-day sequence aimed at a named attorney or litigation operations contact. On day one, send a short email linking a public methodology note to the firm's demonstrated practice and offer a fifteen-minute scoping conversation. On day four, make one manual business call or leave a concise voicemail. On day seven, send a LinkedIn message only where platform rules and the contact's preferences permit it. On day eleven, share one relevant public-data limitation the firm may encounter. On day sixteen, offer a bounded paid validation sprint with a sample deliverable index. On day twenty-one, close the loop and stop unless invited to continue. Do not attach accusations, name prospective relators, or describe sealed matters. Commercial email must satisfy applicable CAN-SPAM requirements under 15 U.S.C. § 7704, including accurate headers, an appropriate postal address, and a working opt-out honored within the statutory period. Avoid automated calling or texting without the required permissions. Inbound publishing should show reproducible methods, provenance standards, and anonymized data-quality lessons, not target lists. A focused webinar for healthcare litigators can generate better questions than broad claims about discovering fraud. Track each channel separately to learn where actual paid buyers originate.

Treat conversion benchmarks as planning hypotheses until actual cohorts mature. An illustrative first campaign begins with three hundred raw firm records, resolves duplicates and practice fit to one hundred twenty qualified accounts, and reaches one hundred named contacts. Twenty positive responses produce twelve discovery calls, eight scoped proposals, four paid pilots, and three signed recurring mandates. The stage rates are 40%, 83.3%, 20%, 60%, 66.7%, 50%, and 75%, respectively; the end-to-end raw-record conversion is 1%. These are testable targets, not market averages. Define a positive response as interest in discussing a relevant paid assignment, excluding courtesy replies and unsubscribes. A win requires a signed scope and initial payment, not merely a favorable call. The four pilots and three resulting mandates represent four customer relationships if mandates upgrade existing pilots; do not report seven distinct clients. Repeating an equally productive cohort three times would yield nine recurring clients, but capacity and market saturation can change the result. Use months one and two for methodology and list validation, months three through six for pilots, and months seven through twelve for renewals and referrals. First paid work may arrive within the specified 4–12-month window, while award collection remains outside that acquisition promise.

Handle objections by reducing uncertainty, not by predicting recoveries. When counsel says, 'We already have analysts,' offer a bounded overflow task using their preferred output schema and a measurable turnaround. When they say, 'Public data cannot make our case,' agree that screening is not pleading support and propose a paid source-gap assessment with an explicit stop condition. When they request contingency-only work, explain that the operating product is forensic delivery purchased on ordinary service terms; counsel must separately assess any lawful award interest, eligibility, professional-conduct restrictions, and conflicts. When price is challenged, reduce cohort size or source count rather than quietly removing provenance checks. A $2,500 pilot with twenty delivery hours costs $1,200 in illustrative labor at $60 per hour plus $300 in data and quality assurance, leaving $1,000 contribution before acquisition costs and general overhead. Fifty-percent upfront billing yields $1,250 cash, not the entire project margin. Define acceptance around reproducibility, completeness against the scope, and timely delivery rather than a favorable case conclusion. Ask for a recurring mandate only after the firm identifies repeated work worth purchasing. With permission, request an introduction that describes service quality without exposing matter facts or implying a paid referral arrangement.

sections.heading: 4. Reconcile cash economics, capacity, and award risk before expanding acquisition
paragraphs: Reconcile every scenario to Formula v2.0 without treating government recoveries, client damages, procurement value, or alleged tax underpayments as operator revenue. The Conservative case is $95,000 annual operator revenue, $64,600 operating costs, and $30,400 owner net profit at 32%, supported by one full-time operator and two contractors. An illustrative service-only bridge is five clients paying $1,500 monthly for twelve months, plus $5,000 of separately earned project work. The Base case is $487,500 revenue, $268,125 costs, and $219,375 owner profit at 45.0%, with one full-time operator and two contractors. Ten clients paying $3,750 monthly generate $450,000; another $37,500 of completed project work reaches the canonical total. The Scaled case is $880,000 revenue, $369,600 costs, and $510,400 owner profit at 58%, with two full-time staff and three contractors. Sixteen clients paying $4,250 monthly generate $816,000; $64,000 of additional earned projects completes the bridge. These mixes illustrate annualized operating states, not a claim that every client signs on January first. A midyear start produces fewer billed months. Keep optional procurement brokerage outside these bridges and maintain a separate ledger for any lawful, realized net statutory award interest.

Protect margin by specifying workloads before selling subscriptions. For the Base bridge, cap each $3,750 monthly mandate at twelve scheduled delivery hours plus defined automated monitoring, with separately priced expansions. Ten clients consume one hundred twenty scheduled hours monthly before quality assurance, acquisition, administration, and project work. Two contractors are scheduled resources, not unlimited capacity; document their availability, specialties, and access permissions. For the Scaled bridge, sixteen mandates at eight scheduled hours consume one hundred twenty-eight hours monthly, leaving the larger team room for deeper project work and control functions. Higher pricing must reflect demonstrated monitoring value and standardized outputs, not unexplained hourly inflation. Treat these caps as illustrative package designs, then measure actual delivery time and renewal behavior. Require written scope changes for new datasets or expanded entity populations. Publish the startup capital envelope of $10,000–$45,000 and the monthly operating overhead range of $1,500–$9,500, but do not mistake that overhead range for total scenario expense. Canonical annual costs must also absorb applicable labor, delivery, acquisition, and other operating costs. Manage runway from collected service cash, staged purchases, and receivable aging. An invoice awaiting payment cannot fund payroll merely because a pending matter has a large alleged recovery.

Statutory awards require program-specific arithmetic. FCA relator shares generally range from 15–25% when the government proceeds and 25–30% when it does not, subject to statutory qualifications and exceptions. SEC awards generally range from 10–30% of qualifying monetary sanctions collected when statutory conditions, including the covered-action threshold, are met. IRS § 7623(b) generally provides 15–30% of collected proceeds subject to its eligibility rules, including the amount-in-dispute threshold and the additional gross-income condition for individual taxpayers. Do not advertise a universal 15–30% rate across these programs. For illustration, a qualifying $10 million FCA recovery at a 20% share yields $2 million to the relator before relevant deductions, not automatically to the analytics company. If the operator has no lawful entitlement, operator award revenue is zero. If an entitlement exists, model only the operator's documented retained share after applicable allocations; never gross up another party's recovery. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to service billings where relevant and obtain appropriate accounting treatment for award interests rather than assuming identical recognition rules. Release no uncollected award into operating cash projections. Expand acquisition only when paid delivery, repeat purchases, receivable collection, and documented capacity jointly support the next cohort.

sections.heading: 1. Contract for evidence production before opening a recovery pipeline
paragraphs: Start with the customer, not the allegation. The paying customer is a plaintiff or relator law firm purchasing defined forensic work: source acquisition, entity resolution, claim testing, chronology construction, and reproducible exhibits. Record the contracting firm, authorized matter contact, permitted sources, delivery milestones, invoice schedule, and restricted recipients before ingesting records. The Base package contains five documented work blocks at $1,625 each, producing an $8,125 monthly engagement. Five concurrent engagements yield $40,625 monthly recognized service revenue when all twenty-five blocks are delivered. A block ends with a reproducible query, source manifest, exception explanation, and counsel acceptance record; it does not promise a complaint or recovery. Price revisions follow additional records or analytical complexity rather than the size of an alleged government loss. Separate the services agreement from any eligible individual's award claim. An analytics company does not acquire statutory whistleblower eligibility merely by buying public records or signing a percentage contract. Counsel determines eligible claimants and permissible arrangements; the accountant determines recognition and principal versus agent presentation. Funds belonging to a client, relator, provider, or government remain outside operator revenue, even when the operator prepares the calculations.

Build intake from CMS Part B and Part D releases, Open Payments, SAM.gov procurement records, and lawfully obtained import manifests. Preserve release date, retrieval time, source URL, license restrictions, content digest, and the exact transformation version. Aggregate billing variation is a lead, not a false claim. Compare specialty, geography, patient mix, billing year, ownership, and reporting thresholds before assigning analyst time. A high percentile becomes actionable only after a plausible innocent explanation has been tested and primary records support the relevant payment representation. Counsel then evaluates 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4), including whether qualifying public disclosures and original-source facts defeat or preserve the proposed action. Public datasets neither automatically establish that bar nor automatically satisfy its exception. For Rule 9(b), build representative-claim packets with dates, actors, statements, payment context, and supporting documents, applying the controlling circuit's pleading standard. Track missing claim-level evidence as a reason to pause, not permission to manufacture specificity. The operator produces a referenced analytical hypothesis; licensed counsel controls the legal theory, investigation demands, and any filing. Keep rejected hypotheses and counterevidence so later reviewers can distinguish a tested allegation from selection bias.

The supplied mapped play, hospital_lien_medical_receivables_arbitrage, requires a separate commercial-claims lane. Assume one hundred denied or underpaid claims contain $2,000 each in potentially recoverable differences: the review pool is $200,000, not revenue. If a recovery partner collects forty percent, provider collections equal $80,000. A twenty-five percent contingency produces $20,000 of that partner's fee revenue, leaving $60,000 for the provider before other agreed charges. The usual twenty-to-thirty-five percent range would produce $16,000 to $28,000 on the same collections. Our forensic operator recognizes only its separately contracted $8,125 service package, where earned, rather than also counting the partner's fee. Federal No Surprises Act IDR covers eligible out-of-network disputes, not every denial; ground ambulance services are generally outside its federal surprise-billing protections. Check service eligibility, the thirty-business-day open-negotiation period, and the subsequent four-business-day initiation window under 45 CFR § 149.510, including applicable extensions. For lapsed or ineligible disputes, evaluate timely ERISA administrative appeals, plan terms, standing, and state remedies. ERISA group-health procedures generally provide at least 180 days to appeal an adverse benefit determination. Signed BAAs, encrypted EDI transport, access logging, and minimum necessary datasets precede protected-health-information processing.

sections.heading: 2. Install an idempotent ledger with evidence holds and atomic posting
paragraphs: The six reference modules below form one executable Python namespace when their code cells are concatenated in order. They use only SQLite and Python standard-library components. Provision one database per contracting firm on a supported local filesystem; do not place the live journal on a shared network mount. Initialize once, then allow separate worker processes to open independent connections. Every business mutation begins with BEGIN IMMEDIATE, checks its command fingerprint inside that transaction, and commits the journal, state transition, and replay result together. SQLite serializes writers, eliminating read-check-write races within this interface. A crash before commit leaves nothing posted; a crash after commit permits the same command to return its stored result. Reusing a command key with different arguments raises an error rather than accepting a second interpretation. A busy timeout may still expire; retry the identical command after bounded delay, never invent a replacement key. UNIQUE constraints protect source fingerprints, evidence attestations, journal identities, and transition identities. The reference deliberately excludes bank transfers and court submissions: database atomicity cannot make an external service execute exactly once. Those actions require their own provider identifiers and independently reconciled acknowledgments.

Intake accepts an immutable source snapshot and derives its fingerprint from the source locator plus content digest. Scoring combines anomaly, corroboration, and provenance inputs on a transparent hundred-point scale; it ranks work rather than estimating legal success. Store full source material in encrypted object storage and put only digests, opaque identifiers, and verification events in this demonstration database. The evidence function records hashes of signed review artifacts. Its caller must already be authenticated and authorized by the surrounding application; a hash proves consistency, not truth or professional status. Verification requires both source and counsel attestations. The escrow_hold state means documentary release restrictions on a potential award, not permission for this business to hold client money. Release requires award payment evidence, an allocation worksheet, and an accounting review. Ordinary retainer billing can continue during that award hold because its consideration comes from delivered services. Keep statutory filing decisions outside the scoring function. Counsel handles FCA complaints under seal, SEC Form TCR, and IRS Form 211. Store sealed materials in separately restricted counsel-controlled repositories; ordinary customer dashboards receive only authorized operational status and no restricted allegations or docket attachments.

Use integer cents throughout the ledger. An invoice debits receivables and credits service revenue only after the corresponding work is delivered; a collection debits cash and credits receivables without creating revenue again. A credit reverses an uncollected invoice amount, while a paid expense debits operating expense and credits cash. The example forbids collections or credits above the matter's outstanding balance and posts eligible award receipts only after documentary release. It does not implement advance deposits, taxes, payroll liabilities, refunds, or client trust accounting; add their complete balanced-entry paths before using those transaction types. Access to direct database writes must remain restricted because SQL privileges can bypass application invariants. The reconciliation view separately exposes earned fees, received awards, cash receipts, paid expenses, receivable movement, and operating cash movement. QA checks journal balance, minimum posting completeness, foreign keys, and negative matter receivables within one consistent transaction. Reconcile cash postings to imported bank statement identifiers and actual bank balances outside this compact reference. Run restored-backup tests and independent access reviews before production. The technical objective is narrow and testable: repeated authorized requests cannot duplicate postings, and concurrent requests cannot overspend an outstanding receivable.

RECONCILIATION = """
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS monthly_reconciliation AS
SELECT
    j.period,
    -SUM(CASE WHEN e.account = 'service_income' THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS service_revenue_cents,
    -SUM(CASE WHEN e.account = 'award_income' THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS award_revenue_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.account = 'ar' THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS receivable_change_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.account = 'cash' AND j.kind = 'collection'
             THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END) AS service_receipts_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.account = 'cash' AND j.kind = 'award'
             THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END) AS award_receipts_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.account = 'expense' THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS paid_opex_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.account = 'cash' THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS operating_cash_change_cents,
    -SUM(CASE WHEN e.account IN ('service_income','award_income','expense')
              THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END) AS operating_profit_cents
FROM journal j JOIN entry e ON e.journal_id = j.id
GROUP BY j.period;
"""

def install_reconciliation():
    db = connect()
    try:
        db.executescript(RECONCILIATION)
    finally:
        db.close()

def monthly_rows():
    db = connect()
    try:
        cursor = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM monthly_reconciliation ORDER BY period"
        )
        columns = [item[0] for item in cursor.description]
        return [dict(zip(columns, row)) for row in cursor.fetchall()]
    finally:
        db.close()

sections.heading: 3. Price legal attrition explicitly and keep award upside outside payroll
paragraphs: Use a probability tree to expose attrition without dressing assumptions as observed DOJ rates. For sensitivity testing, begin with one hundred investigative prospects. Assume sixty fail counsel's combined public-disclosure and original-source assessment, leaving forty; assume half of those lack sufficient representative-claim support, leaving twenty potential filings. These are planning assumptions, not published dismissal frequencies. Among filed matters, assume forty percent intervention and sixty percent non-intervention. Apply an additional ten percent government-dismissal assumption within the non-intervened branch, then assume recoveries in fifty percent of intervened matters and twenty percent of surviving non-intervened matters. Conditional recovery probability becomes 0.40 × 0.50 + 0.60 × 0.90 × 0.20 = 30.8 percent per filed matter. Consequently, 69.2 percent of filed matters and 93.84 percent of initial prospects produce no modeled recovery. Expected branch counts may be fractional because this is a sensitivity model, not an actual docket inventory. Replace assumptions with the operator's observed cohorts and dated DOJ statistics where comparable denominators exist. Granston-style dismissal consideration is distinct from non-intervention: declining intervention does not itself dismiss an action. Track dismissal motions, orders, withdrawals, settlements, and judgments separately.

Award percentages require program-specific arithmetic. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(d), an ordinary eligible FCA relator generally receives fifteen to twenty-five percent when the government proceeds and twenty-five to thirty percent when it does not, subject to statutory qualifications and reductions. A $1 million qualifying recovery therefore supports illustrative gross relator ranges of $150,000 to $250,000 or $250,000 to $300,000, not an automatic analytics-company entitlement. SEC awards generally range from ten to thirty percent of monetary sanctions collected in qualifying actions exceeding $1 million; CFTC percentages also generally run ten to thirty percent. IRS section 7623(b) generally provides fifteen to thirty percent of collected proceeds when its eligibility and amount thresholds apply, including the individual-taxpayer income condition. Thus fifteen to thirty percent is not a universal cross-program rate. Maintain a separate allocation worksheet showing the statutory recipient, collected award, permissible deductions, other owners' interests, and operator amount actually earned. Where the operator acts as agent, ASC 606 presentation reflects the retained service consideration rather than gross custodial receipts. Have the accountant identify the applicable recognition framework for each award; do not assume every statutory payment is customer-contract revenue.

Plan for FCA investigations that may remain under seal for two to five or more years through extensions, while recognizing that SEC and IRS processes have different confidentiality structures rather than an identical court-seal mechanism. Section 3730(b)(2) establishes the initial FCA seal and government service requirements; counsel manages extensions, permitted disclosures, and court directions. A seal breach can cause severe sanctions or dismissal and destroy economic upside, but automatic dismissal is not the universal rule after State Farm Fire & Casualty Co. v. United States ex rel. Rigsby. Keep deadline alerts free of sealed allegations and restrict contractor access to the minimum authorized material. Model a zero-award year as the ordinary operating budget. The Base business remains viable because $487,500 of delivered retainer work covers $268,125 of annual operating costs and leaves $219,375 owner profit. A delayed complaint, declined intervention, or failed award application therefore changes the contingent register rather than payroll funding. If a firm stops purchasing analytical work, reduce its next service allocation and replace that commercial demand independently of litigation outcomes. Never discount invoices against an anticipated relator share or borrow against a probability tree presented as if it were an enforceable receivable.

sections.heading: 4. Walk three monthly cohorts from screened leads to reconciled cash
paragraphs: This ninety-day cohort begins with an established firm roster, not a cold launch. The four-to-twelve-month first-deal range remains the acquisition planning assumption; startup capital of $10,000 to $45,000 funds that separate ramp. Begin this walk with $20,000 unrestricted cash and $20,312.50 opening receivables from delivered Month 0 work. Five ongoing law-firm customers each commission one $8,125 monthly package. Each month produces twenty screened investigative prospects: twelve are scrubbed for weak evidence or innocent explanations, three enter unresolved research holds, and five become paid evidence-production assignments. These counts are illustrative service-selection decisions, not the separate statutory probability tree. Deliver twenty-five blocks by the monthly acceptance date, recognize $40,625, and invoice the five firms. Contracts schedule half of each invoice for payment within that month and half during the following month. Both installments follow delivery, so no advance-deposit liability is needed in this example. The first month collects $20,312.50 from Month 0 and $20,312.50 from Month 1. Each subsequent month repeats that timing, maintaining $20,312.50 closing receivables without treating opening receivables as new current-period revenue.

Allocate $22,343.75 monthly operating costs to the actual production model: $12,000 for two contractors, $4,000 for data acquisition and research infrastructure, $2,500 for security, insurance, and professional administration, $2,000 for business development, and $1,843.75 for other delivery expenses. Contractor labor totals $144,000 annually; the remaining $124,125 brings annual costs to $268,125. For this cohort, all expenses are paid in the month incurred, and the one full-time owner takes profit rather than an additional salary charged on top of the modeled costs. The supplied $1,500-to-$9,500 monthly opex range is an early operating reference, not a ceiling on the mature Base case's fully loaded costs. The example's non-contractor costs are $10,343.75 monthly, making that distinction explicit rather than forcing incompatible budgets together. Retainer receipts of $40,625 minus $22,343.75 paid costs generate $18,281.25 monthly operating cash. No statutory award is collected. Owner distributions, income taxes, capital expenditure, and financing movements are excluded from this operating bridge and must be added separately to an actual bank reconciliation. Opening cash therefore reaches $38,281.25, $56,562.50, and $74,843.75 after Months 1, 2, and 3.

Close each monthly cohort with four reconciliations: accepted blocks to invoices, invoices and credits to receivables, bank transactions to collections and expenses, and ledger totals to the scenario workbook. Across ninety days, fifteen paid assignments produce seventy-five accepted blocks and $121,875 recognized service revenue. Thirty-six prospects were scrubbed and nine remain research holds; neither category generates invoices merely for appearing in the pipeline. Receipts total $121,875 because opening and closing receivables are equal, not because all quarterly invoices have already cleared. Expenses total $67,031.25, leaving $54,843.75 profit and operating cash generation. Multiplying these quarterly figures by four reproduces the Base scorecard exactly: $487,500 revenue, $268,125 costs, $219,375 profit, and a 45.0 percent margin. A missed $20,312.50 installment would reduce cash by that amount and increase receivables equally, before any collectability adjustment; it would not create a statutory award funding source. Suspend new discretionary blocks when overdue balances exceed the contract's credit terms. Reprice or reduce the next cohort if delivery cost rises. The repeatable asset is a verified, paid production system, not a larger inventory of allegations awaiting a distant government decision.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #48, Data-Mined Qui Tam, SEC & IRS Whistleblower Analytics, ranks #16 of 49 with a 92/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This resource directory supports the volume's 11 mapped plays by turning public anomalies into reproducible research, not unsupported allegations. Its operating spine combines CMS utilization, Open Payments, HRSA registrations, procurement records, corporate disclosures, and counsel-controlled corroboration. The canonical annual owner profits are $30,400 Conservative, $219,375 Base, and $510,400 Scaled. Keep recurring law-firm retainers separate from contingent awards, which can take years or return zero. Prioritize stable identifiers, dated source copies, representative claims, and documented alternative explanations. Spend commercial-data dollars only where a targeted purchase resolves an evidentiary gap that free official records cannot close.

sections.heading: 1. Build an official-source spine before purchasing enrichment
paragraphs: Start with a source register, not a scraper collection. Give every dataset an owner, published release date, observation period, access route, permitted use, identifier vocabulary, and reproducible retrieval recipe. CMS Medicare Physician and Other Practitioners and Medicare Part D Prescribers support peer comparisons, but their public files are aggregated, delayed, and subject to suppression. They do not supply the claim-level encounters needed to establish individual false submissions. Preserve both service year and publication date so an apparent utilization jump does not become a fabricated contemporaneous signal. Use NPPES for NPI identity resolution, not proof of active licensure or specialty competence. Match HRSA OPAIS registrations using identifiers and effective periods rather than organization names alone. Open Payments adds reported manufacturer relationships; it does not independently establish improper inducement. Build comparisons within specialty, geography, site of service, beneficiary mix where available, and dataset coverage. A physician with 400 observed services against a peer median of 100 has a fourfold screening ratio, not fourfold recoverable damages. Record the denominator, suppressed observations, and plausible clinical explanations beside that ratio before selling any research memo to counsel.

The first eight entries below anchor a sixteen-source directory continued in Section 2. Each access method names a real entry point while avoiding guessed dataset identifiers or fabricated commercial prices. For CMS APIs, obtain the dataset UUID and version from the catalog's API documentation, then store that resolved endpoint in the acquisition manifest. Prefer published bulk files for full-population work; use filtered API requests for incremental validation. Annual CMS utilization releases cannot support daily surveillance merely because a downloader runs nightly. NPPES monthly dissemination files and weekly updates have different jobs: initialize from a full snapshot and reconcile documented changes afterward. Open Payments publication and correction cycles also require version comparisons rather than blind replacement. For SAM.gov, distinguish entity registrations, contract opportunities, and exclusion records; access permissions and API quotas differ. USAspending award transactions are not invoices or proof of payment for particular defective goods. Read source-specific documentation before joining dates, amounts, and recipient identifiers. Where an API fails, retain the last successful snapshot with an explicit age field and switch to the listed official download rather than silently interpreting an empty response as zero activity.

Use a conservative acquisition scheduler built with urllib.request, json, csv, sqlite3, hashlib, and datetime. Keep secrets in environment variables, never in evidence exports. Apply per-host concurrency limits, bounded retries, exponential backoff with jitter, and Retry-After handling; do not evade throttling through rotating accounts or addresses. Identify the client where the publisher requires it. Preserve response status, retrieval time in UTC, content type, request parameters, final URL, and SHA-256 digest alongside the original bytes. A digest proves that a stored object matches its recorded digest, not that the publisher's assertions were true. Separate immutable source objects from normalized tables and analyst annotations. Validate expected columns, identifier lengths, row counts, date ranges, and duplicate keys before releasing a snapshot to analysis. Set a quarantine state for schema drift or truncation, with a human-readable reason and last working release. Replaying a 10,000-row sample through yesterday's and today's parser should produce explainable differences, not unexplained entity churn. Budget staff time for source changes even when access costs nothing; a free portal with brittle exports can cost more than a narrow, well-documented commercial lookup.

sections.heading: 2. Purchase narrow corroboration instead of indiscriminate enrichment
paragraphs: Run enrichment as an evidence waterfall: official identifier lookup, official relationship verification, targeted commercial corroboration, then counsel-directed primary records. SEC EDGAR provides filings and structured company facts; its reporting perimeter is public issuers and other filers, not every private supplier. GLEIF links legal-entity identifiers and reported parent relationships, but an absent LEI does not imply a fictitious business. State corporate registries, county land records, and professional boards remain jurisdiction-specific corroboration sources. Preserve the exact registry record and its effective date rather than copying a search-engine snippet. Commercial tools such as Panjiva and ImportGenius can identify shipment patterns and intermediaries, but manifest coverage varies by transport mode, jurisdiction, confidentiality treatment, and vendor processing. A consignee-name match needs address, timing, and product corroboration before becoming an ownership or origin assertion. Never infer customs underpayment from a shipment estimate alone. Request lawful entry documents, classification support, and duty calculations through counsel when those facts become material. Source licensing also matters operationally: a subscription may permit internal analysis while restricting redistribution of raw records in client exhibits. Resolve that distinction before promising a downloadable evidence bundle.

Set purchase thresholds against research yield rather than marketing coverage. An illustrative $600 monthly enrichment budget allocated to twenty disputed entity matches costs $30 per resolved inquiry if all twenty resolve; if only five resolve, the effective cost becomes $120. Track accepted matches, rejected matches, unresolved matches, analyst minutes, and downstream evidentiary use separately. Do not treat an available email address as a useful litigation fact. SEC acquisition requires an identifying User-Agent and observance of the published fair-access ceiling of ten requests per second; choose a lower local ceiling and honor later publisher changes. CourtListener and RECAP provide useful docket discovery, but coverage depends on contributions and does not replace the official court record. PACER commonly charges $0.10 per page, subject to applicable caps, exceptions, and quarterly waivers; confirm the current fee schedule before bulk retrieval. Sealed material is not available for public enrichment. Do not probe sealed docket endpoints, infer permission from an exposed URL, or send client matter names to commercial search systems without authorization. A documented inability to obtain a primary record is a research limitation, not permission to invent its contents.

FOIA is a corroboration channel, not a claim-level data vending machine. Build narrow requests around agency, record type, office, date interval, contract identifier, and desired electronic format. The statutory twenty-working-day determination framework is not a promise of completed production; consultations, exemptions, litigation, and backlogs can extend the actual timeline. Record the tracking number, acknowledged scope, fee category, fee ceiling, correspondence, and appeal deadline. Expect privacy and law-enforcement exemptions to affect healthcare and investigative records. IRS return information is restricted by 26 U.S.C. § 6103; public tax-exempt organization records do not open private taxpayer accounts. Use IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search to verify status and retrieve available filings, then distinguish reported organizational revenue from the operator's own fees. Where requests stall, narrow the requested record set, seek already published agency material, or suspend the hypothesis pending lawful corroboration. The directory intentionally mixes free official sources, metered court access, and quote-based commercial services. Their roles are complementary, not interchangeable. Require each paid source to identify a specific missing fact, a permitted use, and a cheaper fallback before renewing the subscription.

sections.heading: 3. Convert anomalies into claim-ready evidence, including the 340B mapped play
paragraphs: Implement the pipeline as four separately testable layers: acquisition, identity resolution, hypothesis testing, and evidence packaging. SQLite is sufficient for a small desk when indexes cover NPI, UEI, award identifier, NDC, and effective dates. Use decimal.Decimal for currency and explicit units for quantities; a dollar obligation, prescription count, dosage unit, and drug package cannot share an unlabeled amount column. Track source-to-output lineage through deterministic transformation versions and parameter files. Diagnostic tests should detect join multiplication, identifier collisions, stale registrations, unexpected null fields, and unexplained distribution shifts. A join that turns 1,000 prescriptions into 1,300 matched rows requires reconciliation before any margin calculation. Produce an exception ledger with source references, reason codes, reviewer disposition, and correction history. For every shortlisted allegation, construct a claim matrix identifying actor, conduct, date, payment request, alleged falsity, supporting record, and competing explanation. Rule 9(b) requires particularity in alleging fraud; jurisdiction-specific pleading standards determine what representative claims or reliable indicia suffice. Public aggregate outliers cannot substitute for that assessment. The paid product is a reproducible research package with explicit evidence gaps, not a machine-generated accusation dressed as a complaint.

Unpack section_340b_contract_pharmacy_spread_arbitrage as a research and controls subject, not presumed misconduct. HRSA-qualified covered entities include eligible health centers, Ryan White entities, and qualifying hospitals; eligibility depends on the applicable statutory category. The play combines TPA split-billing, specialty fulfillment, and referral capture, but none establishes a lawful patient relationship by itself. The often-cited 25–50% or greater acquisition discount is a screening assumption, not a universal statutory percentage. Actual 340B ceiling prices follow statutory pricing mechanics and are not generally available as a public NDC price feed. Illustratively, $10,000 of collected reimbursement less $6,000 acquisition cost, $250 dispensing expense, $150 administration, and $100 transaction expense leaves $3,500 before other costs and reversals. One hundred eligible paid fills produce $350,000 of illustrative program contribution, not analytics-desk revenue. A separately contracted $150 administrative fee per fill would generate $15,000 for that service provider before its expenses, but does not belong in this volume's retainer scorecard. Flat fees do not automatically resolve anti-kickback concerns, payer restrictions, or referral issues. Counsel must evaluate the actual services, remuneration, and relationships.

Test the 340B hypothesis with dated OPAIS relationships, authorized dispensing transactions, encounter evidence, payer terms, acquisition records, and Medicaid billing treatment. CMS Part D summaries alone cannot identify which fills used 340B inventory or establish duplicate discounts. Separate diversion risk under 42 U.S.C. § 256b(a)(5)(B) from duplicate-discount risk under § 256b(a)(5)(A), and distinguish fee-for-service Medicaid identification from managed-care arrangements. Manufacturer contract-pharmacy restrictions and litigation require current, jurisdiction-specific review. The operational fallback is an eligible entity-owned specialty pharmacy alongside permitted contract pharmacies, not a workaround that changes patient eligibility. Where applicable manufacturer arrangements use 340B ESP, automate only authorized claims submissions, reconcile acknowledgments, and verify whether affected NDC access actually resumes; uploads do not assure unrestricted supply. Enforce EHR encounter checks before replenishment and isolate patient records from public analytics storage. Tele-referrals require documented clinical relationships and lawful referral arrangements, not automated capture for margin alone. If access or eligibility fails, stop affected replenishment, investigate exceptions, and price the engagement as controls analysis rather than projecting recoveries. This preserves a billable service even when the suspected abuse does not survive corroboration.

sections.heading: 4. Fund the desk with retainers and treat statutory recoveries as contingent
paragraphs: Reconcile operations to the canonical Formula v2.0 totals without treating a client's reimbursement, government award, or alleged damages as desk revenue. Conservative revenue of $95,000 less $64,600 expenses produces $30,400 owner profit at 32%; Base revenue of $487,500 less $268,125 produces $219,375 at 45.0%; Scaled revenue of $880,000 less $369,600 produces $510,400 at 58%. Staffing remains 1 FT + 2 C, 1 FT + 2 C, and 2 FT + 3 C respectively. The table supplies illustrative retainer-led revenue mixes that reproduce those totals with zero award receipts; these mixes are planning constructions, not additional canonical inputs. Startup capital remains $10,000–$45,000, monthly opex guidance $1,500–$9,500, and first-deal timing 4–12 months. That opex range cannot represent all scaled expenses: reconcile labor, contractors, project delivery, and other modeled costs separately without double counting. Separate billed fees, recognized service revenue, receivables, and collected cash. If an operator acts as agent for another service provider, evaluate ASC 606 principal-versus-agent presentation and recognize only its retained consideration where appropriate. Never gross up the desk's revenue using pharmacy reimbursement or the government's recovery.

Use an award sensitivity ledger outside the operating budget. FCA relator shares generally span 15–25% when the government proceeds and 25–30% when it does not, subject to statutory qualifications and reductions. SEC awards generally span 10–30% under their qualifying framework; IRS mandatory-program awards generally span 15–30% subject to thresholds and reductions; CFTC generally uses 10–30%. These regimes do not share one universal percentage. An analytics vendor receives no statutory entitlement merely by finding an anomaly or supporting a law firm. Model only the operator's established entitlement, after applicable deductions, and distinguish it from lawyer compensation. FCA investigations can involve 2–5+ years under seal; other award programs also have long timelines but do not use the identical court-seal mechanism. An illustrative $2 million collected recovery times a 20% eligible share equals $400,000 before deductions, not current revenue. A 25% assumed probability of reaching that outcome gives $100,000 of undiscounted sensitivity value, still zero spendable cash before collection. Keep probability-weighted research economics separate from recognized revenue, bank balances, and staffing commitments.

Model legal attrition with explicit branches rather than a universal win rate. Screen 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4) public disclosure and original-source issues, Rule 9(b) pleading sufficiency, intervention, non-intervention, government dismissal, merits outcomes, and collection separately. For an illustrative stress test, assume 70% non-intervention and a 10% dismissal branch within that cohort: 100 candidate matters then yield 70 non-intervened matters and seven modeled dismissals, before other losses. These are deliberately hypothetical rates, not measured DOJ or Granston-era frequencies. Replace them with dated, cohort-defined observations where available; annual DOJ statistics alone may not supply matched outcome denominators. Government dismissal under § 3730(c)(2)(A) is distinct from declining intervention. Zero collection must remain a supported scenario after years of work. FCA complaints go exclusively through licensed relator counsel under § 3730(b)(2); counsel also routes SEC Form TCR and IRS Form 211 submissions. Maintain matter-specific access, sealed-document isolation, and counsel-controlled communications. A seal violation can cause serious sanctions and jeopardize recovery, but automatic forfeiture is not a universal rule. Stop external sharing whenever the permitted disclosure scope is unresolved.
