sections.heading: 1. Establish Counsel-Led Eligibility Before Pricing an Evidence Dossier
paragraphs: Start with a service engagement, not a promise to manufacture a whistleblower claim. The law firm hires the operator to reconcile datasets, preserve source records, test alternative explanations, and document reproducible findings. Counsel decides whether facts support liability under 31 U.S.C. § 3729 and whether a proposed relator can proceed under § 3730. An unusually high CMS payment ratio is a research lead, not proof that a false claim reached the government. Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 9(b) requires particularity for allegations of fraud; circuit approaches differ on when reliable indicia can substitute for representative claim details. Build a claim-level worksheet recording provider identity, service date, billing code, payer, challenged representation, corroborating record, and competing explanation. Leave unsupported propositions out of the deliverable rather than filling gaps with statistical confidence. Record whether each fact came from CMS Part B/D, Open Payments, SAM.gov, import manifests, an authorized witness, or a client-owned record. A $7,500 monthly retainer purchasing 30 analyst hours implies $250 per hour before overhead; its invoice becomes payable for delivered analysis regardless of whether counsel files anything. That separation makes negative findings commercially useful and removes pressure to characterize every anomaly as fraud.

Public-source mining creates a specific eligibility problem under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4), not a blanket prohibition on public information. Counsel must compare substantially similar allegations or transactions against the statute's enumerated public-disclosure channels and assess the original-source exception and government's opposition authority. Preserve publication dates, acquisition dates, independent knowledge, and any qualifying voluntary disclosures to the government. Also screen the first-to-file restriction in § 3730(b)(5), limitations under § 3731(b), and materiality under Universal Health Services v. Escobar. All FCA complaints in this operating model are filed exclusively through licensed relator counsel. Section 3730(b)(2) requires an initial seal of at least 60 days, service on the government of the complaint and written disclosure of substantially all material evidence, and no service on the defendant until ordered. Extensions can produce long investigations; a 2–5+ year filing-to-payment horizon does not mean every case remains sealed throughout that period. Never place a sealed caption, target name, allegation, or case-specific search query into an enrichment vendor. A seal breach can produce serious sanctions and jeopardize recovery, but dismissal or loss of an award is not an automatic statutory consequence of every breach.

Separate each award program before discussing percentages. FCA shares generally run 15%–25% when the government proceeds and 25%–30% when it does not, subject to statutory qualifications and reductions. SEC awards generally run 10%–30% of monetary sanctions collected in qualifying covered and related actions, with covered actions requiring sanctions exceeding $1 million. IRS § 7623(b) generally provides 15%–30% when its proceeds and taxpayer thresholds are met; discretionary § 7623(a) claims follow a different framework. CFTC awards likewise generally use 10%–30%, not a universal 15%–30% band. Route SEC Form TCR and IRS Form 211 submissions through counsel as a firm operating requirement, without implying counsel is universally mandated by those programs. Anonymous SEC submissions seeking eligibility require attorney representation under the applicable rules. A vendor does not earn a statutory award merely by selling a dossier, and its entity eligibility cannot be assumed across programs. Document the actual claimant, qualifying knowledge, submission timing, assistance duties, and payment recipient. Have counsel assess prior reporting obligations and original-information exclusions before acceptance. If eligibility fails, retain the ordinary paid analytics engagement only where independently valuable; remove contingent upside from that matter's forecast and stop describing the vendor as an entitled whistleblower.

sections.heading: 2. Contract for Deliverables, Lawful Access, and State-Specific Boundaries
paragraphs: Use a master services agreement plus a matter-specific statement of work signed by the retaining law firm. Define the service as forensic data analysis and litigation support, expressly reserving legal opinions, representation, claim selection, and filing decisions to licensed counsel. List included datasets, permitted joins, deliverable formats, analyst hours, acceptance tests, and excluded investigative activity. A defensible acceptance test reproduces five sampled calculations from preserved source files; it does not require counsel to agree that fraud occurred. State the fee trigger as a monthly service period or accepted milestone, with a specified invoice date, payment term, and change-order mechanism. Prohibit percentage compensation tied to attorney fees unless applicable professional rules expressly permit the arrangement; California Rule of Professional Conduct 5.4 illustrates the nonlawyer fee-sharing problem. Contingent litigation-support or expert compensation raises additional state and evidentiary concerns. Do not disguise a referral fee as an analytics success fee. Any separately eligible claimant award requires its own counsel-reviewed treatment and must never be assumed assignable to the vendor. Require the client to identify its contracting entity, authorized instructor, billing contact, and evidence-transfer channel so payment disputes cannot become leverage over testimony, regulatory reporting, or access to a client's own records.

State boundaries follow the actual work, not the contract's chosen label. California Business and Professions Code § 6125 and New York Judiciary Law § 478 restrict unauthorized practice; a vendor should not tell a prospective relator which claims to plead or negotiate representation as though it were counsel. Investigative licensing needs a separate analysis. California Business and Professions Code § 7521 broadly describes private-investigator activities, while Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1702 and Florida Statutes Chapter 493 impose their own structures and exceptions. Desk research is not automatically exempt because its inputs are public, and retention by a lawyer does not create a universal exemption. Before witness contact, surveillance, identity tracing, or evidentiary investigation, obtain a written jurisdiction-and-activity assessment from counsel or use an appropriately licensed subcontractor. Add separate assessments for state false-claims statutes, local filing procedures, and sector restrictions; state remedies do not simply inherit federal eligibility or seal rules. For healthcare matters, distinguish published aggregate CMS information from identifiable patient records. Access to the latter requires a lawful basis and role-specific analysis under HIPAA and applicable state law. Neither a public billing anomaly nor a whistleblower label authorizes downloading an employer's entire clinical database.

Allocate intellectual property and custody explicitly. The client receives its source records, matter-specific work product, and a documented license or ownership interest in paid deliverables; the operator retains preexisting parsers and generalized methods without retaining confidential matter facts for resale. A confidentiality clause should preserve legally protected government reporting and must not require prior notice or permission where that would impede SEC communications under 17 CFR § 240.21F-17. Contracts governing confidential information with employees and covered contractors should include the immunity notice contemplated by 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b), while making clear that its conditions do not authorize unrestricted acquisition. Specify security controls, breach notification, subcontractor access, retention, litigation holds, and return or deletion procedures. Counsel-directed work may support privilege or work-product protection, but a legend alone does not establish either. Negotiate a liability cap with explicit treatment of confidentiality breaches, intentional misconduct, and data misuse, and confirm enforceability under selected state law. Dispute clauses should identify forum, escalation, and preservation duties while allowing protected reporting and necessary emergency relief. Narrow anti-circumvention to identified commercial introductions for a defined period; never restrict government cooperation, witness access, a client's counsel choice, or a whistleblower's statutory communications.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile Retainer Cash, Award Uncertainty, and the API Waterfall
paragraphs: Keep the Formula v2.0 scorecard unchanged and expose its economics before building a pipeline forecast. Conservative revenue of $95,000 less $64,600 of modeled costs equals $30,400 owner profit at 32%; Base revenue of $487,500 less $268,125 equals $219,375 at 45.0%; Scaled revenue of $880,000 less $369,600 equals $510,400 at 58%. Teams remain 1 FT + 2 C, 1 FT + 2 C, and 2 FT + 3 C respectively. An illustrative revenue bridge, not an additional canonical assumption, allocates Conservative to $95,000 services and zero awards, Base to $450,000 services plus $37,500 eligible realized awards, and Scaled to $780,000 services plus $100,000 eligible realized awards. Five firms paying $7,500 monthly generate the Base service component; ten paying $6,500 generate the Scaled component. At unchanged costs and zero awards, those two illustrations still produce $181,875 and $410,400, distinct from the canonical profit cases. Government recoveries, client damages, tax assessments, and attorney receipts are never operator revenue. Recognize only revenue attributable to the operator under applicable accounting rules; accountant-reviewed principal-versus-agent and variable-consideration treatment governs service arrangements. A realized award component belongs here only when the modeled operator is actually entitled to that income and recognition is appropriate.

Model statutory downside explicitly rather than multiplying every anomaly by a headline award percentage. For FCA matters, use conditional branches for eligibility after § 3730(e)(4) review, survival of Rule 9(b) pleading, intervention or non-intervention, government dismissal, merits recovery, collection, and actual claimant allocation. Section 3730(c)(2)(A) supplies government dismissal authority; United States ex rel. Polansky v. Executive Health Resources addresses dismissal after intervention. The Granston memorandum concerns dismissal factors, not a statutory award formula or a universal dismissal rate. No cohort rates are supplied here. Calculate observed non-intervention and dismissal rates only from a dated, defined sample, stating denominators, observation windows, unresolved cases, and overlap between events. Do not subtract overlapping percentages as independent losses. Stress every matter with zero recovery and delayed collection beyond five years; probability-weighted pipeline estimates remain separate from cash available for payroll. Multi-year DOJ investigations, non-intervention, discovery costs, and adverse merits decisions can eliminate or defer the entire award component. Use the stated $10,000–$45,000 startup range and $1,500–$9,500 monthly operating-expense range as planning inputs, not proof that all annual staffing costs fit inside that monthly band. Require collected retainers to cover committed operating outflows before adding award-dependent capacity.

The supplied play free_tier_api_waterfall_multiplexing supports law-firm prospect enrichment, not transmission of sealed evidence. Aggregate 30–60+ independent B2B data, email-verification, firmographic, DNS, and SERP providers only where their permanent developer tiers permit the intended commercial use. Forty providers offering 250 lookups each create 10,000 nominal monthly calls, not 10,000 guaranteed usable records. At two upstream calls per cache miss, 4,000 enrichment requests with 60% valid cache hits consume 3,200 calls before retries. Ten customers at $199 monthly produce $1,990 monthly or $23,880 annual billings within the play's $99–$499 price range; include that amount inside service revenue if used, never on top of the canonical totals. Near-zero upstream charges still leave hosting, validation, support, and licensing costs. Maintain 40+ interchangeable adapters, Postgres cache provenance, retention limits, and quota telemetry. When quotas tighten, prefer permitted local cache hits and lawful public-web, DNS, or MX extraction; otherwise reduce throughput or buy an authorized tier. Never rotate accounts to evade limits or resell restricted provider output. Across the volume's 11 mapped plays, apply this same source-rights and unit-cost discipline; only this supplied identifier receives play-specific economics here, avoiding invented mappings for the remaining ten.

sections.heading: 4. Use Outreach That Sells Analysis Without Soliciting Restricted Evidence
paragraphs: Aim initial outreach at law firms, using public practice descriptions and firm-level contact details rather than purchased lists of alleged victims or employees. Commercial B2B email remains subject to 15 U.S.C. § 7704: accurate routing and subject information, required advertising identification, a valid physical postal address, a clear opt-out mechanism, and timely suppression are operational requirements. The sender should append its actual business identity and postal address before sending; an example script is not a substitute for those particulars. Use this body verbatim after confirming its factual accuracy: 'I provide reproducible forensic analysis of public CMS, Open Payments, procurement, and trade records for plaintiff-side counsel. The engagement purchases source-linked analysis, including explanations that weaken a theory; it does not purchase a promised claim or recovery. Would a 20-minute discussion of your team's research backlog be useful? Please do not send client identities, sealed allegations, or confidential documents in reply. Reply stop to end these commercial messages.' Use the subject 'Forensic research capacity for counsel.' Honor opt-outs within ten business days and keep the suppression record separate from prospect enrichment. Avoid target-specific accusations, recovery projections, misleading government affiliations, and statements suggesting that counsel must act before an invented deadline.

Discovery should establish authority, scope, and payment before facts migrate across systems. Use this opening: 'Which attorney will supervise the engagement, which jurisdiction governs the intended work, and what decision should the analysis support? Please describe the dataset categories without naming a sealed matter. Are you requesting public-source analytics, review of records your client may lawfully provide, or licensed investigative activity? We price a defined service milestone independently of any filing or award.' Then ask: 'What existing disclosures or proceedings might affect eligibility, what representative claim evidence can counsel authorize us to examine, and what innocent explanation would change your assessment?' Do not ask employees to retrieve records beyond their access rights, bypass controls, or upload another person's credentials. If someone volunteers sensitive material, use this response: 'Please stop transmitting documents here. A licensed attorney should assess your authority to possess and disclose them and provide an appropriate channel. We can discuss our service without receiving those materials.' For phone outreach, assess 47 U.S.C. § 227, FCC rules, state calling restrictions, and applicable recording law before using automation or recording. California Penal Code § 632 and Florida Statutes § 934.03 illustrate why a single nationwide recording script cannot replace jurisdiction-specific analysis.

Close with a written discovery recap that the supervising attorney can correct before access is provisioned. Use this scope confirmation: 'The proposed pilot costs $2,500 for ten analyst hours, a source register, one reproducible anomaly test, and a competing-explanation memorandum. It excludes legal opinions, witness contact, complaint drafting, and submission. Payment purchases the work whether the result supports, weakens, or eliminates the proposed theory. Additional work requires a written scope change.' This is an illustrative pilot quote, not a replacement for the annual scorecard. If asked for an award split, respond: 'Our service fee is independent of attorney compensation and government recovery. Counsel must assess any separately eligible claimant interest; we do not sell eligibility or promise a percentage.' If a prospect asks for a sealed-case example, respond: 'We can demonstrate methods using public or synthetic records, not restricted matter details.' Maintain one outreach register with source provenance, message version, suppression status, and authorized follow-up date. Keep it segregated from the evidence repository. Review sample messages quarterly for unsupported claims and provider-derived personal information. A defensible growth channel produces paying counsel relationships while keeping allegations, claimant identities, and confidential evidence out of prospecting systems entirely.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #48, Data-Mined Qui Tam, SEC & IRS Whistleblower Analytics, ranks #16 of 49 with a 92/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter maps 11 operator plays into a counsel-facing evidence factory: conditional startup credits, three anomaly engines, corroboration, extraction, qualification, seal tracking, and three distribution loops. Python handles repeatable transformations; people decide identity, evidentiary sufficiency, confidentiality, and release. The Conservative, Base, and Scaled annual owner-profit cases remain $30,400, $219,375, and $510,400. Retainers fund operations while contingent awards stay outside spendable cash until realized. A timed batch model targets 74% repetitive-work automation without removing reviewer accountability. Public-disclosure screening, representative-claim gaps, non-intervention, dismissal, and zero recovery determine which promising anomalies never become filings.

sections.heading: 1. Build a replayable anomaly engine before adding model capacity
paragraphs: Treat the business as a reproducible research service, not an allegation generator. Map eleven chapter operating plays to owned queues; the credit play retains its supplied identifier, while the other ten names describe this chapter's implementation rather than additional catalog identifiers. Plays two through four are CMS anomaly detection, Open Payments relationship resolution, and procurement/import corroboration. A Python scheduler downloads authorized CMS Part B and Part D releases, Open Payments bulk files, SAM.gov records, and lawfully licensed manifest extracts. Use urllib.request for bounded downloads, csv and gzip for streaming, hashlib for fingerprints, and sqlite3 for job state. Write each source into an immutable landing directory with acquisition time, release date, license reference, schema version, and SHA-256 digest. Never interpret an absent or suppressed CMS cell as zero activity. Separate provider identifiers from names, preserve historical addresses, and attach a confidence score to every proposed join. Partition records by reporting period before calculating peer comparisons so revised releases cannot silently rewrite an earlier dossier. The owner reviews exceptional joins; one contractor maintains ingestion, while another reconstructs source evidence. A failed download produces a stale-source warning and pauses dependent scoring rather than recycling yesterday's results as fresh evidence.

The first mapped play, cloud_ai_startup_credit_aggregation_arbitrage, belongs in the capacity budget, not the revenue forecast. A genuine Delaware or Wyoming operating company may apply through verified incubator, venture-partner, or founder-perk channels to AWS Activate, Microsoft's startup programs, Google Cloud for Startups, Cloudflare, OpenAI, and Anthropic where current eligibility permits. The supplied $25,000–$350,000 opportunity range describes potential programs and combinations, not an entitlement or an additive balance every applicant receives. Record actual award letters, expiration dates, service exclusions, affiliation rules, and restrictions on overlapping benefits. Do not manufacture shell entities to repeat an offer, resell API keys, or move a client dossier merely to consume credits. Budget the illustrative batch at $12 undiscounted machine expense; if $8 is eligible and valid credits cover it, cash machine expense becomes $4 until exhaustion. Maintain the $12 shadow cost for pricing. Each entity must operate a genuine standalone vertical product with defensible separation. A preprovisioned local open-weight service using an appropriately licensed Llama or DeepSeek model behind vLLM can preserve extraction capacity, but memory limits, licenses, and benchmark results determine suitability. Tested failover reduces interruption; it does not make migration instantaneous or eliminate hardware expense.

Score behavior within relevant peer groups rather than ranking raw billing totals. CMS features might include procedure mix, beneficiary-adjusted intensity, and year-over-year changes, with specialty and geography held constant where the source permits. Open Payments features identify relationships for review, not proof that a payment induced a claim. Procurement and manifest features compare award timing, shipping descriptions, country fields, and contract requirements; a consignee name alone cannot establish importer responsibility or domestic-origin misrepresentation. Price these three engines as one reusable batch: 40 candidates consume the illustrative $12 machine budget, or $0.30 each, before human work. Deduplicate on source identifiers and reporting windows, then attach explanations showing which records changed the score. Implement signed incoming webhooks with hmac, timestamp checks, idempotency keys, payload limits, and replay rejection; the webhook only enqueues work. Use a durable outbox for notifications so a restarted worker cannot issue duplicate client messages. Missing schemas move to quarantine, suspicious entity matches require review, and rate-limit responses trigger bounded exponential backoff with jitter. When a vendor feed disappears, retain the dated last-good snapshot for historical comparison, label its age prominently, and stop generating claims about current conduct.

callout.title: Make every attractive anomaly cheap to disprove
callout.body: The durable asset is a repeatable evidence trail that survives a skeptical counsel review, not a large pile of model-generated suspicions.
items: Preserve both original and revised CMS releases; a revision can explain an apparent utilization discontinuity before counsel spends interview time.
Keep separate observed, inferred, and disputed relationship fields in Open Payments joins; never let a confidence score overwrite the source identity.
Buy manifest coverage only after testing whether the required shipper, consignee, date, and commodity fields exist for the selected trade lane.
Set credit-expiration alerts at sixty and thirty days, then test the paid and local routes using public documents before protected work depends on them.

sections.heading: 2. Automate corroboration and dossiers without manufacturing evidence
paragraphs: Play five is the FOIA and primary-source corroboration builder. Convert each candidate into a question ledger: alleged mechanism, relevant period, missing records, possible innocent explanation, and the exact record that could resolve the uncertainty. FOIA under 5 U.S.C. § 552 provides access procedures and exemptions, not an immediate production promise or a substitute for discovery. Generate draft requests naming custodians, date ranges, record types, and preferred electronic formats; a person approves scope and submission because the request itself communicates information outside the firm. Track acknowledgment, tracking number, fee correspondence, production batches, and appeal dates without treating the statutory determination period as a delivery deadline. For each produced file, preserve the original, extract text into a separate derivative, and log redactions and missing attachments. Budget $2 of the $12 machine batch for retrieval orchestration and indexing; fees and licensed records are separately authorized expenses inside the engagement budget. If an agency withholds documents, record the asserted exemption and route the decision to counsel. Switch to accessible primary sources, narrow the hypothesis, or close the candidate rather than filling evidentiary holes with an LLM's plausible reconstruction of records it has never seen.

Play six is citation-bound extraction and dossier assembly. A model receives only approved document excerpts, a constrained field schema, and instructions to return quoted spans with page or row locators. Treat embedded document instructions as hostile content: they cannot request secrets, change destinations, invoke tools, or amend the extraction contract. Parse returned JSON with strict size and type checks; validate every quoted span against stored text before it enters the evidence ledger. Python's stdlib handles orchestration, JSON, and hashing; PDF parsing and OCR require separately selected services or local executables rather than pretending they exist in the stdlib. Budget $4 for model extraction, $3 for approved OCR or parsing, and $3 for storage, scoring, and orchestration, including the $2 corroboration allocation already described. Those categories total $12 rather than adding a second retrieval charge. Prepare an evidence packet containing source inventory, chronology, entity map, competing explanations, and unresolved questions. A deterministic template supplies headings and source links when the model fails. No model invents missing invoices, beneficiary details, contract clauses, interviews, or representative claims. Counsel receives an explicitly incomplete packet when decisive documents remain unavailable, with each unsupported proposition removed from the factual narrative.

Play seven is counsel-fit qualification, with an explicit separation between statistical interest and filing sufficiency. The full-time owner checks practice focus, jurisdiction, conflicts routing, available evidence, engagement economics, and willingness to pay for bounded support work. Counsel assesses the FCA public-disclosure bar under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4), including the statutory channels of disclosure, substantially similar allegations, original-source requirements, and the government's ability to oppose dismissal. Publicly accessible data does not automatically create a viable relator, and neither does it automatically resolve the statutory analysis. Build a Rule 9(b) matrix linking who, what, when, where, and how to actual source passages; representative-claim demands and acceptable alternatives vary by circuit and factual context. Aggregate CMS summaries often cannot establish claim submission, falsity, or knowledge. The model flags missing elements but never declares them satisfied. For four accepted packets from forty candidates, the illustrative $272 fully loaded batch costs $68 per accepted packet; rejection of all forty is a valid outcome, not permission to lower standards. If counsel declines, retain the reason, stop external circulation, and reuse only nonconfidential method lessons rather than shopping an identifiable allegation across a mailing list.

sections.heading: 3. Fund the service with retainers and isolate contingent recovery
paragraphs: Play eight is the counsel-controlled litigation-support and seal tracker. Store matter identifiers, named access holders, counsel instructions, deadlines, and authorized export history in a separate protected workspace. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(b)(2), FCA complaints are filed by licensed relator counsel under seal, initially for at least sixty days, with statutory government service and disclosure requirements; extensions can continue far longer. Do not synchronize protected matter titles into ordinary CRM records, public issue trackers, shared calendars, model telemetry, or marketing analytics. A reminder uses an opaque identifier and points authorized counsel to the protected record. Retain the actual sealing order because restrictions are matter-specific. A seal breach creates serious litigation and recovery risk, but dismissal or share loss is not mechanically automatic in every case. Route SEC Form TCR and IRS Form 211 through counsel under this operating model, with separate program-specific intake and deadline rules. Never transplant the FCA seal process onto those programs. The often-cited 2–5+ year horizon describes possible investigation and recovery delays, not a universal seal duration or an expected payment date. If instructions conflict or access fails, suspend exports and seek counsel's clarification while preserving the audit trail.

Reconcile the canonical Formula v2.0 cases using a retainer-only cash planning bridge with zero realized awards. Conservative revenue is five firms at $1,500 monthly for twelve months, plus $5,000 of separately scoped support: $95,000 revenue less $64,600 costs equals $30,400 owner profit and 32% margin. Base revenue is eight firms at $4,500 monthly plus $55,500 support: $487,500 less $268,125 equals $219,375 and 45.0%. Scaled revenue is ten firms at $6,500 monthly plus $100,000 support: $880,000 less $369,600 equals $510,400 and 58%. These illustrative contract mixes reproduce the supplied totals; they do not assert an observed customer roster. The first two cases use 1 FT + 2 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 3 C. Costs include contractor delivery, research, infrastructure, acquisition, insurance, and other operating expenses rather than merely cloud invoices. Recognize support revenue as services are delivered under the applicable contract treatment. Client recoveries, healthcare payments, shipment values, and government loss estimates are not operator revenue. Only a lawfully entitled, realized net award share belongs in the award ledger; principal-versus-agent assessment under ASC 606 prevents presenting another party's gross recovery as the operator's sales. A service contract cannot manufacture statutory whistleblower eligibility.

Stress-test the award pipeline independently of that operating bridge. In an illustrative cohort of one hundred leads, remove thirty after public-disclosure analysis and twenty more for unresolved particularity defects, leaving fifty counsel-selected matters. Assume 80% non-intervention, leaving forty such matters and ten interventions. Apply a 25% government-dismissal sensitivity to the forty, leaving thirty; assume recovery in 20% of those thirty and 60% of the ten interventions. Only twelve original leads recover; eighty-eight produce zero recovery. These are deliberately hypothetical sensitivity inputs, not measured DOJ non-intervention or Granston dismissal rates. The historical Granston memorandum concerns government dismissal practice; operative authority is 31 U.S.C. § 3730(c)(2)(A), subject to governing procedure and case law. Counsel should replace assumptions with dated, relevant evidence without conflating non-intervention with dismissal. FCA shares generally range from 15%–25% with intervention and 25%–30% without, subject to statutory qualifications. SEC and CFTC awards generally use 10%–30% ranges subject to qualifying conditions, while IRS section 7623(b) generally uses 15%–30% with its own thresholds and reductions. Thus one universal 15%–30% multiplier is wrong. Even eligible awards remain zero in spendable cash until collection; test the entire year with no awards and delayed retainer receipts before hiring.

callout.title: Four checks before a consequential release
callout.body: An automated score can open a review task. Only accountable people may authorize an allegation-bearing export, filing instruction, or protected disclosure.
items: Verify source hashes, entity identities, exact quotation support, and the unresolved-evidence register before releasing any factual dossier.

sections.heading: 4. Compound safe distribution and measure automation net of rework
paragraphs: Play nine is programmatic methods publishing, not automated accusation publishing. Produce pages explaining dataset coverage, reporting lags, suppression, entity resolution, and reproducible validation techniques using synthetic examples or carefully selected public material cleared for reuse. Python can generate static pages, sitemaps, and structured download manifests; a reviewer approves every new template and checks sampled outputs for accidental identifiers. Play ten is permission-aware counsel outbound: build a small list from public professional directories, score practice fit, and draft individualized capability messages without attaching case allegations. Apply 15 U.S.C. § 7704 requirements where applicable, including accurate headers, required sender information, a functioning opt-out, and timely suppression. Do not scrape restricted directories or evade sending limits. Play eleven is the counsel referral and reusable-tool loop: a useful source-coverage worksheet travels between practitioners and links back to a booking page, without exporting client matters. Price the distribution experiment at $240 monthly tools plus six human hours at $60, or $600 total. If one paying engagement results, acquisition cost is $600 before additional sales work; if none results, record the full loss and change the audience or offer rather than inflating lead quality with automated volume.

Measure the 70%+ target against a frozen repetitive-work baseline, not against all professional judgment. In one illustrative forty-candidate batch, manual collection takes 300 minutes, normalization 180, initial qualification 160, packet drafting 220, and routing preparation 140: 1,000 minutes total. Automation removes 250, 160, 110, 180, and 40 minutes respectively, totaling 740 minutes or 74%. The remaining 260 minutes include verification, exceptions, and recipient checks; at $60 per hour they cost $260, plus $12 machine expense, or $272 per batch. That is $6.80 per candidate and $68 per accepted packet if four qualify. The timed scope excludes attorney pleading work, specialist interviews, and bespoke investigations, which require separate pricing. Counsel-fit software assists rather than replacing the attorney's statutory analysis. At one hundred, one hundred fifty, and two hundred annual batches, direct batch expense is $27,200, $40,800, and $54,400 respectively, already included within the scenario cost envelopes. These volumes are capacity illustrations, not additional revenue assumptions. Require two successive measured cycles above 70% after corrections; if identity errors or packet rework consume saved time, report the lower achieved rate and restrict automation to the transformations that remain reliable.

Close the flywheel with quality signals that cannot leak case strategy. Store channel source, broad practice category, booked consultation, signed retainer, renewal, and reviewer rework minutes in the commercial CRM; keep allegation text and evidence inside the protected matter workspace. A client-approved, nonidentifying methods improvement can become a worksheet update, which attracts another counsel conversation and supplies better qualification questions. Never describe a live sealed matter as a success story or circulate a supposedly anonymous pattern that identifies the parties. Define operational service objectives for data freshness, replay completion, citation validity, and access revocation. Test restoration using synthetic dossiers, rotate webhook secrets, and rehearse a queue backlog with outbound delivery disabled. When an API, model, or source changes, pin the last validated pipeline, route uncertain packets to manual review, and communicate revised delivery dates rather than silently degrading accuracy. Startup capital of $10,000–$45,000 and monthly opex of $1,500–$9,500 are planning ranges, not substitutes for the fully loaded annual scorecard costs; delivery intensity and contractor expense can make those totals much larger. With first deals potentially four to twelve months away, size runway from actual cash commitments. Scale reviewers before increasing outreach whenever the exception queue exceeds contracted turnaround capacity.

chapters.pull_quote: Automate the search for evidence, never the decision that an allegation is ready to travel.
action_checklist: Create an immutable source manifest for CMS, Open Payments, SAM.gov, and authorized manifest inputs, then test schema quarantine and replay.
Implement all eleven mapped operating plays with named owners, undiscounted unit costs, permitted inputs, and documented failure fallbacks.
Benchmark a forty-candidate batch against the 1,000-minute baseline and count reviewer corrections before reporting automation above 70%.
Require source-bound quotations, public-disclosure analysis, Rule 9(b) gap review, and counsel-authorized recipients before dossier release.
Reconcile $95,000, $487,500, and $880,000 annual revenue cases to their exact costs and profits while holding uncollected awards at zero cash.
Launch one cleared methods worksheet, a narrowly targeted counsel outreach cohort, and a referral loop that excludes protected matter details.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you structure a lean 1 FT + 2 C (3 people) -> 2 FT + 3 C (5 people) pod, enforce weekly scorecards, and build transferable books that command a premium exit multiple (or durable cash cow)?
chapters.title: Pod Architecture, Contractor KPIs & Exit Valuation
chapters.subtitle: Counsel Retainer Pods, Evidence QA, ASC 606 Cohorts, Written IP Assignments & Transferable Earnings
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #48, Data-Mined Qui Tam, SEC & IRS Whistleblower Analytics, ranks #16 of 49 with a 92/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its 11 mapped plays belong inside one evidence-production system, not eleven speculative case factories. Start with one full-time principal and two contractors; expand to two full-time employees and three contractors only when collected retainers support the added capacity. Canonical annual owner profits are $30,400 Conservative, $219,375 Base, and $510,400 Scaled. Separate paid litigation-support delivery from contingent awards, enforce reproducible evidence and written IP ownership, and cap each customer or economic counterparty at 25% of recurring revenue. Buyers pay for transferable contracts and replacement-adjusted earnings, not allegations, sealed docket counts, or headline government recoveries.

sections.heading: 1. Assign Eleven Plays to Three Seats Before Adding Capacity
paragraphs: Run Candidate #48 as a forensic services pod whose product is a reproducible, counsel-ready evidence package. For staffing purposes, map its eleven plays into these work packages: CMS Part B anomaly screening; CMS Part D anomaly screening; Open Payments relationship analysis; SAM.gov procurement linkage; import-manifest reconciliation; cross-source entity resolution; FOIA and primary-source corroboration; representative-claim evidence assembly; counsel retainer delivery; sealed-matter milestone administration; and realized-award reconciliation. This is the chapter's operating allocation, rather than a claim that every dataset establishes an actionable violation. The principal owns scoping, engagement economics, customer communication, and acceptance. The data contractor owns ingestion, normalization, linkage, and reproducible transformations. The evidence contractor owns source verification, request tracking, contradiction searches, and dossier assembly. Licensed counsel remains responsible for legal theory, filing decisions, procedural obligations, and permitted disclosures; the pod does not become a law firm by employing excellent analysts. Give every work package one accountable seat, one reviewer, a delivery definition, and an access classification. A shared job register connects the source snapshot to the client engagement, contractor purchase order, acceptance record, and invoice. That register is both the production backbone and the first artifact a serious acquirer should examine.

In the three-person configuration, reserve the principal's calendar for selling a narrow deliverable, resolving exceptions, reviewing evidence, and collecting invoices. Do not fill that calendar with manual spreadsheet repair. The two contractors should review each other's mechanical work where competent, while the principal arbitrates material defects and counsel evaluates legal sufficiency. At five people, add a full-time delivery lead and a third contractor specializing in claims reconstruction or source-specific verification. The delivery lead assumes scheduling, acceptance records, and customer reporting; the principal retains pricing and capital allocation. Contractors are fractional capacity, not three concealed full-time salaries. Use written scopes and independent deliverables, and evaluate worker classification under the actual federal and state tests. Set a 25% ceiling for each law-firm customer and each common-control economic counterparty on trailing-twelve-month recurring revenue. Also inspect outstanding receivables and next-quarter contracted revenue at that threshold. Four equal customers mathematically satisfy the ceiling but leave no operating cushion; target five to eight independently paying firms. During startup, disclose unavoidable concentration, freeze discretionary expansion, and prioritize diversification rather than representing a one-client business as already within policy.

Purchase capacity against accepted work units rather than against the number of allegations generated. An illustrative data-contractor rate of $70 per hour and evidence-contractor rate of $60 per hour, each used eight hours weekly for fifty weeks, consumes $52,000 annually. Against the Conservative scenario's $64,600 total expense envelope, that leaves only $12,600 for every other modeled expense. The calculation exposes how little room exists for expansive software subscriptions, specialist counsel paid by the operator, insurance, and rework. These rates are planning assumptions, not market quotes or extra costs to add after the canonical profit. Negotiate bounded batches with separately priced scope changes, and buy fewer hours when the budget cannot carry the workload. Authorize the five-person configuration only after a thirteen-week cash forecast survives zero awards, a lost major retainer, and a one-month collection delay. Keep at least three months of committed service expenses in unrestricted cash as an internal target. A contractor bench is useful only if replacement analysts can reproduce a sample job without the founder's memory. Document source licenses, join rules, exclusions, and acceptance tests before increasing intake.

callout.title: Protect the Small Pod from Evidence Rework
callout.body: The profitable unit is an accepted, reproducible counsel deliverable, not a large anomaly queue or a speculative recovery estimate.
items: Freeze each CMS release and hash the source files before contractor work begins; rerun only after recording a deliberate release change.
Maintain a negative-evidence field for every flagged provider or vendor so counsel sees legitimate explanations before investing in a theory.
Buy representative-claim reconstruction as a separate bounded task; a population-level outlier chart cannot substitute for transactional particulars.
Keep restricted matter names out of ordinary contractor invoices; use counsel-authorized matter codes and a separately permissioned crosswalk.

sections.heading: 2. Enforce Weekly Quality, Ownership, and Outcome Scorecards
paragraphs: Every Monday, close the prior week's production register before discussing new opportunities. Track accepted packages, first-pass acceptance, material-defect escapes, median cycle time, scope variance, billable utilization, collections, and customer concentration. Define first-pass acceptance as packages accepted without material revision divided by packages submitted that week; show both counts so a tiny denominator cannot masquerade as stable performance. Start with internal targets of 95% first-pass acceptance, zero unsupported material assertions, and 100% source traceability. These are management targets, not observed industry benchmarks. Reconcile delivery counts to accepted milestones and invoices instead of rewarding activity such as rows scraped or leads generated. Use Git for code history and an appropriately permissioned document repository for evidence; keep secrets and restricted documents outside ordinary repositories. Each exception needs an owner, cash impact, next action, and due date. The principal reviews receivable aging and contracted workload alongside quality, because an immaculate package for a nonpaying customer does not finance the pod. Publish a compact internal scorecard, then send each law firm only its own authorized service report, with legal assessments supplied by counsel rather than inferred from analyst metrics.

Contractor compensation should purchase competent analysis, not a desired accusation or a government recovery. Use hourly ceilings or fixed batch prices, with objective acceptance criteria and payment dates stated before work starts. An illustrative service agreement allows two business days for routine review, one business day to acknowledge a material defect, and three business days to deliver a correction plan. Source outages and scope changes pause the delivery clock through a written change record, not an informal excuse. Pay for accepted contracted work even when counsel rejects the legal theory; negative findings can be excellent work. Avoid recovery-based analyst bonuses that encourage overstatement or create additional fee-sharing questions. Secure a signed present assignment of identified deliverable copyrights under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), plus appropriate confidentiality, invention, and subcontractor flow-down terms. Do not assume every contractor work product qualifies as work made for hire. Inventory preexisting code, licensed datasets, and open-source components separately, specifying the rights actually granted. Public facts are not made proprietary by placing them in a spreadsheet. Verify that the contract permits reuse of general methods without permitting reuse of client evidence, confidential strategy, or restricted source material.

Maintain a second, restricted outcome scorecard for counsel-led matters without converting it into a sales leaderboard. Record referrals, counsel acceptances, filed cohorts, intervention decisions, government dismissal motions, final dismissals, collections, and elapsed months. Explicitly calculate the DOJ non-intervention rate as declined intervention decisions divided by resolved intervention decisions within a defined filing cohort. Calculate the government-initiated dismissal-motion rate and final-dismissal rate separately, using stated denominators and observation dates. The Granston memorandum concerns DOJ dismissal considerations; it does not supply a universal probability applicable to this pod. Use documented DOJ statistics or counsel-verified cohort records when available, and label immature cohorts as censored rather than treating pending matters as wins. Neither non-intervention nor a dismissal motion mechanically determines the final recovery. For capital planning, however, run a zero-recovery case and a full-delay case in which no contingent receipt arrives within the forecast horizon. Public-disclosure problems, weak representative claims, adverse merits, and procedural failures each belong in the loss taxonomy. Never pay a contractor more for suppressing those categories. A useful scorecard shows why a package failed, whether the service was still contractually earned, and which production step will change before the next delivery.

sections.heading: 3. Keep Retainer Cash, Award Cohorts, and Statutory Exposure Separate
paragraphs: Preserve the Formula v2.0 totals exactly: Conservative revenue of $95,000 at 32% yields $30,400 owner profit; Base revenue of $487,500 at 45.0% yields $219,375; Scaled revenue of $880,000 at 58% yields $510,400. The corresponding total expense envelopes are $64,600, $268,125, and $369,600. Those are annual model totals, not evidence that awards arrive annually or that all expenses recur evenly. The supplied scorecard does not allocate revenue between retainers and realized awards, so maintain that allocation in the actual ledger rather than inventing a canonical split. For a zero-award cash stress test, average monthly collected service revenue must at least cover the relevant committed cash expenses; using the full annual expense envelopes as a simplifying proxy produces $5,383.33, $22,343.75, and $30,800 monthly coverage requirements. Actual payroll dates, taxes, working capital, and noncash charges require a separate cash bridge. Matching the published profits without awards would require the entire respective revenue total to come from services at those same expense levels. The stated $1,500–$9,500 monthly opex range therefore cannot be substituted for the all-in expense envelopes without reconciling labor and every other included category.

Build separate service and award subledgers, each reconciled to the general ledger and bank. Under the applicable revenue policy, a retainer collected before performance can create a contract liability rather than immediate earned revenue; recognize services as the promised work is performed under the engagement's actual terms. Track contracted backlog, earned unbilled work, invoices, credits, cash, and write-offs distinctly. For each award cohort, store filing vintage, claimant identity under restricted access, program, entitlement documents, counsel-approved milestones, authorized deductions, and eventual payment. Do not assume a service firm qualifies as a statutory claimant simply because it produced analytics. Accountants and counsel must establish who owns any award and the accounting basis for amounts the operator actually earns. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis where relevant to service arrangements, and document the applicable policy for statutory receipts separately. If the operator merely handles another beneficiary's proceeds, those pass-through amounts are not its revenue. An applicable retained_share means the operator's entitled net contribution, not the government's total recovery. The scorecard's gross revenue label describes operator revenue before its expenses; it never licenses counting client proceeds, underlying medical spending, or procurement value as operator sales.

Require counsel to assess the FCA public-disclosure bar under 31 U.S.C. section 3730(e)(4) before converting public-dataset findings into a filing thesis. Public availability alone does not resolve that inquiry: the qualifying disclosure channels, substantially similar allegations, original-source provisions, and government position matter. Rule 9(b) requires particularity for fraud allegations, with circuit-specific treatment of representative claims and reliable indicia; build the transaction record counsel requests instead of declaring every statistical outlier a false claim. Counsel files FCA complaints under section 3730(b)(2), including the initial statutory seal and disclosure obligations. Budget a 2–5+ year contingent horizon for long-running investigations and recoveries, potentially including extended FCA seal periods, without asserting that every matter stays sealed that long. SEC and IRS submissions have different confidentiality regimes and are routed through counsel using Form TCR and Form 211. FCA shares generally differ between intervened and non-intervened recoveries; SEC and CFTC ranges are generally 10%–30%, while qualifying IRS awards generally use 15%–30% subject to statutory conditions. Those percentages belong to eligible claimants, not automatically to the analytics pod. Model complete loss and counsel-controlled responses to any suspected disclosure breach.

callout.title: Four Checks Before Capacity Expansion or External Diligence
callout.body: The principal records these checks; counsel resolves legal scope and the accountant resolves recognition questions.
items: Verify that committed contractor work, payroll, and service obligations remain funded when every pending award pays zero.
Verify counsel's public-disclosure analysis, Rule 9(b) evidence requirements, and authorized handling instructions before treating a matter as filing-ready.
Verify signed contributor assignments, source-license rights, and customer-specific transfer restrictions before presenting reusable IP to a buyer.
Verify that each customer and related economic counterparty stays at or below 25% of recurring revenue, with separately documented startup remediation.

sections.heading: 4. Sell Transferable Service Earnings, or Keep a Disciplined Cash Cow
paragraphs: Prepare an exit book that explains how recurring service earnings survive the principal's departure. Buyers will distinguish a repeatable litigation-support provider from a founder who personally persuades three law firms to purchase bespoke investigations. Present customer cohorts, service retention, gross contribution after direct delivery labor, renewal dates, collection history, contractor continuity, and documented acceptance standards. Separate award receipts and one-time projects from recurring service earnings in every bridge. Illustrative negotiation bands for a small, owner-dependent services business might be 2–3 times normalized seller's discretionary earnings; a transferable managed service operation might test 3–5 times normalized EBITDA. These are underwriting assumptions, not sourced transaction comparables or promised clearing prices. A weak transfer package can command less, and a buyer may decline entirely. Do not apply both measures to the same earnings or call owner net profit EBITDA. Reconcile interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, owner benefits, replacement management cost, and recurring delivery expense explicitly. Verify whether replacement labor already sits in expenses before deducting it again. Premium pricing comes from demonstrated continuity and diversified collections, not from describing unresolved allegations as a proprietary pipeline worth a percentage of potential government recoveries.

Use a transparent valuation example independent of the canonical scenario totals. Suppose diligence supports $150,000 of normalized recurring service EBITDA after market replacement management and all recurring delivery costs. At an illustrative 3–4 times multiple, enterprise value is $450,000–$600,000 before debt, cash, working-capital adjustments, transaction expenses, and any contingent consideration. This does not restate the Base case's $219,375 owner profit or imply that the difference is a verified normalization adjustment. Show the actual earnings bridge before using an actual scenario in negotiations. Keep speculative awards outside the base purchase price; if parties consider contingent value, counsel must first establish whether any relevant interest can lawfully transfer and whether disclosure is permitted. A services acquisition does not automatically transfer a relator's standing, an individual's whistleblower eligibility, privilege, or confidential government communications. Design any permitted earnout around clearly defined collections and delivery costs, with reporting rights and dispute procedures. Avoid an earnout that rewards disclosure of restricted material or pressures analysts to amplify allegations. Stress the buyer model for loss of the largest customer and include a realistic transition workload rather than assuming the principal disappears immediately.

Build the transfer room in layers. Begin with aggregate service metrics, redacted contract summaries, ownership schedules, and synthetic demonstration jobs that reveal no restricted matter facts. Counsel determines whether additional client permissions, protective measures, or court action are required before any sensitive disclosure. A buyer confidentiality agreement alone does not override a seal, privilege, client restriction, or source license. Obtain required assignment or change-of-control permissions, and show contractor continuity through written agreements rather than verbal assurances. If sale pricing is unattractive, operate the same system as a durable cash cow: distribute only after taxes, service reserves, working-capital needs, and correction obligations are funded. Reassess concentration quarterly, reprice labor-intensive engagements, and sunset data feeds whose accepted outputs do not cover their full delivery cost. Run an annual founder-absence test in which the delivery lead or designated backup completes a customer reporting cycle without informal founder intervention. At three people, test a shorter documented handover instead of pretending the business has management depth it cannot afford. chapters.subtitle: A Three-Person CMS, Procurement, SEC TCR, and IRS Form 211 Sprint Built Around Paid Counsel Retainers, Claim Particularity, and Restricted Case Evidence
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #48, Data-Mined Qui Tam, SEC & IRS Whistleblower Analytics, ranks #16 of 49 with a 92/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This sprint converts its 11 mapped plays into a three-person operating sequence: acquire permitted records, test anomalies, corroborate representative claims, and sell scoped litigation-support work to qualified counsel. Day 30 proves process quality, not an award pipeline. Day 60 tests buyer commitment; Day 90 tests collected retainer economics before capacity expands. Canonical annual owner profit remains $30,400 Conservative, $219,375 Base, and $510,400 Scaled. A separate cash ledger excludes every uncollected award, while explicit public-disclosure, particularity, non-intervention, dismissal, and zero-recovery branches prevent speculative claims from underwriting payroll.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Bound the eleven plays, staff the pod, and cap exposure
paragraphs: Start with a narrow buyer and one testable fraud theory, not a warehouse of accusations. Candidate #48 uses one full-time operator and two contractors: a data engineer and a forensic reviewer. The founder owns sales, collection, scope, and counsel coordination; the engineer owns reproducible acquisition and joins; the reviewer owns source interpretation and contradiction testing. For this launch, map the eleven plays as P1 CMS Part B utilization, P2 CMS Part D prescribing, P3 Open Payments relationships, P4 SAM.gov award context, P5 permitted import-manifest comparisons, P6 entity resolution, P7 FOIA corroboration, P8 representative-claim reconstruction, P9 counsel retainers, P10 counsel-routed FCA, SEC, and IRS submission support, and P11 restricted-matter tracking. These are working execution labels, not eleven simultaneous product launches. Activate P1, P3, and P6 against one specialty during week one; retain the other lanes as documented adapters. CMS aggregates can indicate a question but cannot independently establish a knowingly false claim. SAM.gov registration is not evidence of a procurement payment, and manifest inconsistencies require shipment-level explanations before escalation. Reserve contractor capacity explicitly: twelve engineering hours and eight reviewer hours weekly, with no case-specific production outside a written scope.

Adopt a $25,000 startup-capital assumption within the canonical $10,000–$45,000 range. Authorize no more than $10,000 of cumulative cash disbursements through Day 30: $6,000 for initial counsel consultation, access controls, equipment, and permitted source acquisition, plus $4,000 of operating expense. The monthly operating envelope allocates $1,800 to engineering, $1,200 to forensic review, $300 to storage and tools, $300 to buyer development, and $400 to contingency. Quoted contractor hours must fit those amounts; otherwise reduce scope before committing work. Maintain the same $4,000 monthly ceiling through Day 90, producing an $18,000 cumulative spend ceiling and $7,000 untouched reserve. These are launch controls, not the annual scorecard expense forecast. Founder living costs and tax reserves need separate funding; do not hide them inside supposed free labor. The stated monthly operating range is $1,500–$9,500, but its upper bound is inappropriate before retainers validate demand. Pay no source for stolen records and buy no access whose permitted uses exclude litigation support. On Day 2, record every recurring charge, cancellation date, contractor commitment, and maximum remaining liability in a cash register that the founder reconciles each Friday.

Build evidence controls before downloading production material. Use Python, SQLite, and SHA-256 manifests for acquisition and transformations, with encrypted storage, individual accounts, multifactor authentication, and a separate workspace per matter. Every extract needs publisher, retrieval timestamp, release version, permitted-use basis, query parameters, and digest. Keep original bytes immutable and log corrections as new versions. Use synthetic examples for sales demonstrations; never expose a prospective client's allegations to another buyer. Counsel must determine privilege arrangements, preservation duties, conflicts, and appropriate disclosure paths before sensitive intake. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(b)(2), an FCA complaint is filed in camera and remains under seal for at least sixty days, with government extensions possible; it is not served on the defendant until ordered. A matter may remain under seal for 2–5+ years, while award collection can take equally long or longer. That planning horizon does not describe SEC or IRS procedures as court-seal systems. Seal violations can imperil a case and its economics, although dismissal is not automatic for every violation. Require counsel's written distribution instructions, restrict matter identifiers, and disable outbound demonstrations using restricted evidence before the first substantive interview.

callout.body: The founder records each result and assigns unresolved items to counsel or the source owner before further handling.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Turn anomalies into reproducible, falsifiable dossiers
paragraphs: Week two converts raw variation into an auditable shortlist. Run P1 and P2 only within comparable specialties, geographies, and reporting periods; payment totals without beneficiary and service denominators create misleading rankings. Join P3 Open Payments using provider identifiers and explicit reporting years, then test whether a relationship predates the relevant conduct. Use P4 procurement records to identify actual award identifiers and modifications rather than treating registration as a contract. P5 manifest comparisons require documented coverage limitations, consignee identity checks, and alternative explanations such as transshipment or classification changes. The engineer produces twenty ranked anomalies, but the reviewer must reject at least every unsupported causal inference rather than satisfy an arbitrary accusation quota. Check a stratified sample of twenty entity joins and require at least nineteen correct matches before producing client materials. Record source completeness separately from anomaly precision: a complete extract can still yield useless leads. Preserve negative controls, such as comparable providers without the flagged relationship, and publish the exact SQL and parameters behind each chart. An operator who cannot reproduce yesterday's ranking should repair the pipeline before contacting any law firm about its findings.

P7 and P8 supply the bridge between a pattern and a counsel-reviewable theory. Submit two narrowly framed FOIA requests for identifiable agency records, tracking request numbers, fee limits, and responses; do not assume statutory response periods mean records arrive during this sprint. For each of three candidate dossiers, identify the asserted representation, actor, relevant date, payment pathway, and primary record that supports or contradicts each element. Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 9(b) requires particularity for fraud allegations; representative claims are a strong operating target, but circuit standards and reliable-indicia arguments differ. Counsel decides whether the evidence satisfies the applicable pleading standard. Separately inventory disclosures under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4), including relevant federal proceedings, federal reports and investigations, and news media. Publicly accessible material is not automatically a qualifying public disclosure, yet a clever recombination of public records does not automatically establish original-source status. Document independent knowledge, timing, and material additions for counsel's assessment. Mark a dossier unqualified when the public-disclosure issue remains unresolved; a high anomaly score cannot erase that defect. Treat corroboration spending as bounded discovery of facts, never as permission to reconstruct missing evidence.

Route each theory into the appropriate program rather than recycling one generic whistleblower packet. FCA relator shares generally run 15%–25% when the government proceeds and 25%–30% when it does not, subject to statutory qualifications and reductions. SEC awards generally range from 10%–30% of qualifying monetary sanctions collected in covered actions exceeding $1 million; original-information and submission rules matter. IRS section 7623(b) generally provides 15%–30% of collected proceeds when its statutory conditions apply, including the amount-in-dispute threshold and the individual taxpayer income condition. CFTC referrals need their own 7 U.S.C. § 26 analysis and are outside this sprint's active filing lanes. Thus the shelf's 15%–30% shorthand cannot substitute for program-specific calculations. P10 prepares counsel-routed Form TCR or Form 211 support, or FCA complaint exhibits; the analytics pod does not submit a qui tam complaint itself. Being a support vendor creates no automatic right to a statutory share. Only a legally eligible claimant's actual entitlement belongs in an award model, and counsel must assess any proposed assignment or compensation arrangement. Sell defined analytical services, not a percentage of a law firm's legal fees.

callout.title: Four habits that make forensic work useful to relator counsel
callout.body: Counsel buys evidence that survives contradiction, provenance questions, and procedural scrutiny, not the largest anomaly count.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Sell bounded retainers and isolate contingent award risk
paragraphs: P9 turns validated analytical capability into a service that plaintiff and relator firms can purchase without waiting for government action. Build a list of twenty firms with relevant practice experience, identify eight suitable buyers, and seek four substantive discovery conversations by Day 30. Offer a $3,000 pilot for one defined dataset, one reproducible anomaly analysis, and one counsel-facing evidence memo, followed by a $4,000 monthly retainer capped at twenty delivery hours. These are illustrative prices, not canonical scorecard inputs or expected first-month receipts. Specify acceptance criteria, revision limits, permitted recipients, source costs, and invoice timing. A commercially qualified conversation includes a responsible buyer, recurring analytical need, procurement path, and budget discussion; an enthusiastic reply alone does not count. Demand advance payment for the pilot before case-specific delivery where the firm's process permits it. Do not buy leads containing confidential allegations or promise access to sealed matters. Measure time spent on proposals separately from delivery so apparent service margins do not conceal unpaid selling effort. The canonical first-deal window remains four to twelve months, so a thirty-day sprint can validate demand without producing a signed retainer or an invoice.

Keep the annual scorecard intact and the launch forecast separate. Conservative revenue of $95,000 minus $64,600 of total costs yields $30,400 owner profit at 32%; Base revenue of $487,500 minus $268,125 yields $219,375 at 45.0%; Scaled revenue of $880,000 minus $369,600 yields $510,400 at 58%. Conservative and Base use one full-time operator plus two contractors; Scaled uses two full-time operators plus three contractors. No supplied allocation divides those totals between retainers and awards, so do not invent one. The revenue label refers to operator revenue, not government recoveries, client damages, sanctions, tax deficiencies, or claimed overpayments. Maintain separate ledger accounts for earned support fees and realized operator-entitled award amounts. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis where relevant to support arrangements and retain only the operator's recognized share when acting as agent; counsel and the accountant determine appropriate treatment of award rights and receipts. Collected cash and recognized revenue need separate columns. A $3,000 advance for unfinished work improves liquidity but is not automatically earned revenue. Every runway calculation assigns zero dollars to uncollected awards and zero dollars to unsigned service proposals, regardless of their perceived probability.

Explicitly stress the award funnel without presenting invented national rates as observed facts. For an illustrative cohort of one hundred theories, assume 60% survive counsel's public-disclosure and source-status screen, and 50% of those satisfy the applicable particularity assessment. Of thirty remaining theories, assume 20% intervention and 80% non-intervention. Apply hypothetical government-dismissal rates of 10% to the intervention branch and 25% to the non-intervention branch, then recovery rates of 50% and 15% to their respective survivors. The result is 2.7 recovery equivalents in each branch, or 5.4 overall; the remaining 94.6 produce no recovery in this model. These conditional assumptions are sensitivity inputs, not current DOJ statistics, and fractional counts represent expected outcomes across repeated cohorts. Granston refers to a DOJ dismissal-policy framework, not a standalone statutory dismissal rate. Government dismissal authority comes from 31 U.S.C. § 3730(c)(2)(A), subject to applicable procedure; non-intervention itself does not terminate a case. Recalculate with zero recovery and a five-year collection delay before considering any award exposure. Only retainers fund operating commitments. Record source, period, denominator, and intervention definitions before replacing hypothetical rates with published DOJ observations.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30: Run the acceptance test and schedule Day 60/90 decisions
paragraphs: Use the final nine days to prove repeatability, not to manufacture a filing deadline. On Day 22, freeze a candidate dossier and ask the reviewer to reproduce it without the engineer's verbal assistance. Day 23 checks every material assertion against its source; Day 24 resolves counsel's distribution and program-routing questions. Day 25 presents the scoped service to qualified buyers, and Day 26 records proposal objections without exposing restricted material. Day 27 reconciles cash, contractor hours, and remaining liabilities. Day 28 tests backup restoration and a simulated misdirected-message response; Day 29 compiles the decision packet; Day 30 records Kill, Fix, or Scale with an owner and deadline. Define dossier completeness as the percentage of required fields containing a supported fact or an explicit, assigned research question; it does not measure legal merit. Require every material factual assertion to have a source regardless of the completeness score. Track reviewer rework as corrective hours divided by total delivery hours. Track join accuracy on a documented sample, not a convenient handpicked subset. A missing representative claim remains a substantive limitation even when every dashboard metric is green.

Decision precedence is simple: a hard stop overrides every commercial metric, and Scale requires every threshold in its row. Kill means terminate the affected acquisition route or business hypothesis while preserving records and honoring existing duties; it never means delete evidence. Stop immediately for unlawful sourcing, inability to protect restricted material, or spending beyond the authorized ceiling. Day-30 Scale means only authorize the next bounded experiment: three reproducible dossiers, 95% sampled join accuracy, 90% dossier completeness, four qualified buyer conversations, and spend within $10,000. With adequate controls but weaker demand, Fix one specialty, offer, or source for fourteen days rather than expanding all three. By Day 60, require eight cumulative qualified conversations, two written scoped proposals, and one buyer-confirmed evaluation timetable for continued commercial expansion. Zero proposals after eight qualified conversations kills the current offer, not necessarily the entire market. The cumulative spending limit becomes $14,000. No award count, filed complaint, or promising counsel reaction can replace those thresholds. Track buyer-confirmed timing in writing and distinguish procurement delay from an offer that solves no funded operational problem.

At Day 90, true delivery Scale requires two paying retainers totaling at least $8,000 monthly, two consecutive months with collected retainer cash covering cash operating expense by at least 1.25 times, and at least 50% delivery contribution margin. Calculate that margin after contractor labor, matter-specific tools, and founder delivery hours valued at $75 per hour; it is not the canonical annual net margin. Require rework of 10% or less and at least three months of unrestricted cash runway after proposed commitments. Under the full-spend, zero-receipt launch case, $7,000 remaining against $4,000 monthly expense gives only 1.75 months of runway and fails that test. If two buyers document viable evaluation dates within ninety more days but receipts lag, choose Fix: reduce monthly spending to $1,500 and reassess without hiring. The remaining $7,000 then covers about 4.67 months, subject to outstanding liabilities. If neither paid demand nor documented evaluation survives, pause the commercial hypothesis. Even when Scale passes, retain the three-person pod until delivery utilization and contracted cash justify expansion; the five-person Scaled scorecard is an annual operating case, not a Day-90 staffing entitlement.
